title: File Association: coordsystems
summary: Defines when to search for an associated file matching 'coordsystem' with extension '.json'.
retrieval_text: The 'coordsystems' association applies when file conditions match the selector rules. Associated files may be inherited from shallower directory levels.

ai_enrichment.description: This association rule defines how BIDS Manager locates the _coordsystem.json sidecar file for EMG recording data (.emg) and electrode description files (_electrodes.tsv). The coordinate system JSON file specifies the reference frame and spatial properties in which electrode positions are expressed.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: When BIDS Manager processes an EMG data file or an _electrodes.tsv file, it automatically searches for a corresponding _coordsystem.json file in the same or parent directories. The rule requires the space entity to match, ensuring that the coordinate system metadata aligns with the spatial reference used for the electrode positions.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Correctly linking electrode positions to their coordinate system is critical for spatial analysis and multimodal integration. BIDS mandates that _coordsystem.json files be inherited rather than duplicated across tasks or runs. This association rule enforces the standard BIDS inheritance lookup, ensuring validators and downstream tools can reliably find the necessary spatial metadata.
example_scenarios: A dataset contains sub-01_electrodes.tsv in the emg/ folder. BIDS Manager looks for sub-01_space-ACPC_coordsystem.json in the same or parent directory to validate the electrode coordinate reference.

Multiple EMG tasks share the same electrode layout. Instead of copying _coordsystem.json into each task folder, it is placed in the emg/ root. The association rule inherits it for all matching EMG files.

Electrode positions are recorded in pixel coordinates on a scalp photo. The _coordsystem.json uses CoordinateSystem: Pixels, and the association links it to the relevant EMG files via the space entity.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Ensure that a _coordsystem.json file exists with a matching space entity in the same directory or a parent directory. Verify that the coordinate system keyword defined in the JSON correctly corresponds to the space entity label used in the filename. If the association does not trigger, check that the file conditions (datatype, suffix, extension) match the selector rules.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: Per the BIDS specification for EMG, _coordsystem.json is required if _electrodes.tsv is specified. The specification strongly recommends against duplicating this file across multiple tasks or runs, relying instead on BIDS inheritance. The space entity typically corresponds to the coordinate system keyword defined in the JSON file.

title: File Association: atlas_description
summary: Defines when to search for an associated file matching 'description' with extension '.json'.
retrieval_text: The 'atlas_description' association applies when file conditions match the selector rules. Associated files may be inherited from shallower directory levels.

ai_enrichment.description: This association rule defines the mechanism for linking a data file containing the 'atlas' entity to its corresponding metadata sidecar. When a file has the 'atlas' entity and a non-JSON extension, the system searches for an associated file with the suffix 'description' and the '.json' extension. This sidecar typically contains structural or categorical metadata about the atlas or parcellation scheme.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: When BIDS Manager encounters a file like 'atlas-MNI152_dseg.nii.gz', it applies this rule to locate 'atlas-MNI152_description.json'. The 'inherit: true' setting means the manager will search for this JSON file in the same directory as the data file, and if not found, will look in parent directories following BIDS inheritance principles. The JSON file provides descriptive metadata rather than acquisition parameters.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Correctly associating atlas files with their description metadata ensures that downstream neuroimaging pipelines can accurately interpret the parcellation scheme, coordinate space, and region definitions. It also prevents validation warnings about missing sidecars and ensures consistent metadata resolution across nested dataset structures.
example_scenarios: A derivative file 'sub-01_atlas-HCP_dseg.nii.gz' exists in 'derivatives/annotations/sub-01/'. The manager searches for 'sub-01_atlas-HCP_description.json' in the same folder. If missing, it inherits the file from 'derivatives/annotations/' due to the 'inherit' flag.

A dataset root contains 'atlas-MNI152_description.json'. All atlas files in any subdirectory (e.g., 'func/atlas-MNI152_dseg.nii.gz') will automatically inherit this metadata, provided no conflicting JSON files exist at intermediate levels.
A user places 'atlas-Brain1_description.json' in the same directory as 'atlas-Brain1_dseg.nii.gz'. The association matches directly, and the local file takes precedence over any inherited metadata.
common_causes: Missing or misnamed '_description.json' sidecar files.
Placing multiple applicable JSON files at the same directory level, which violates BIDS inheritance rules.
Incorrect use of the 'atlas' entity or non-standard suffixes that prevent the association from triggering.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Verify that every file with the 'atlas' entity has a corresponding '<base>_description.json' file. If the JSON is intended to be inherited, ensure it is placed in a parent directory and that no other applicable JSON files exist at intermediate levels. Confirm that the JSON filename matches the data filename's base exactly, differing only by the 'description' suffix and '.json' extension.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: This association aligns with BIDS common principles regarding metadata inheritance. According to the specification, JSON key-values are loaded from the top of the directory hierarchy downwards, and values from shallower levels are inherited by deeper levels unless overridden. There is no concept of 'unsetting' a key-value pair once inherited.

title: Raw File Template: base
summary: Defines filename structure for base raw BIDS files.
retrieval_text: The raw template 'base' defines filename entity requirements. Entities include: subject (required), session (required)

ai_enrichment.description: The "base" template for raw BIDS files defines the foundational naming convention for data files. It mandates the inclusion of the subject entity and allows for the optional session entity, followed by a file-specific suffix and extension.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: In BIDS, every raw data filename must begin with the sub- key-value pair. The session entity (ses-) is appended only when the dataset includes multiple sessions or when the file explicitly belongs to a specific session. The existing record's raw_content correctly marks session as optional, aligning with the BIDS specification, whereas the retrieval_text incorrectly lists it as required. Users should rely on the raw_content definition for validation and file organization.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Adhering to the base template ensures that automated validation tools, processing pipelines, and data repositories can correctly parse and organize files. Incorrect entity usage or missing required entities will cause validation failures and hinder data interoperability across the BIDS ecosystem.
example_scenarios: A functional MRI file from a single session: sub-01_bold.nii.gz
A structural MRI file from the second session of a multi-session study: sub-01_ses-02_T1w.nii.gz
An invalid filename missing the required subject entity: ses-01_bold.nii.gz (fails validation)
common_causes: Assuming the session entity is mandatory for all datasets
Omitting the required subject identifier
Repeating an entity within the same filename (e.g., sub-01_sub-02_bold.nii.gz)
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Verify that all raw data filenames start with sub-<label>. Include ses-<label> only if the data is organized into sessions and the file corresponds to a specific session. Ensure no entity appears more than once in a filename, and that labels use only allowed characters.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: BIDS filenames are constructed as a chain of entities, a suffix, and an extension. Entities must follow a fixed order and cannot be duplicated. The BIDS specification recommends zero-padding numeric labels (e.g., 01 instead of 1) for intuitive alphabetical sorting, though this is not strictly required for uniqueness.

title: Raw File Template: recording
summary: Defines filename structure for recording raw BIDS files.
retrieval_text: The raw template 'recording' defines filename entity requirements. Entities include: acquisition (required), run (required)

ai_enrichment.description: The 'recording' raw file template defines the filename structure and entity requirements for continuous physiological or electrophysiological data (such as EEG, MEG, EOG, ECG, EMG) in BIDS. It specifies which entities are required or optional to uniquely identify each continuous recording file. According to the provided schema, the acquisition and run entities are marked as optional within this template, alongside other base raw entities. The template also governs the use of the recording- entity, which is specifically intended to distinguish continuous recordings from different instruments or with different parameters.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: Users should understand that this template governs how continuous raw data files are named. The optional status of acquisition and run means these entities are not strictly mandatory for every recording file, but should be used when multiple recordings share the same base parameters or occur within the same session to ensure unique identification. The recording- entity is specifically designed for continuous data streams, while run- is used for multiple acquisitions with identical parameters. If different entities (like ses- or acq-) already distinguish the files, run- may be omitted.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Correctly applying this template ensures that continuous data files are uniquely identifiable and consistently organized. Misnaming or omitting necessary entities can lead to validation errors, data loss, or difficulties in downstream processing pipelines that rely on BIDS-compliant filenames to parse experimental design and link data to metadata files like scans.tsv or events.tsv.
example_scenarios: A subject undergoes two EEG sessions with identical parameters. The files are named sub-01_ses-01_task-rest_acq-EEG_run-1_eeg.vhdr and sub-01_ses-01_task-rest_acq-EEG_run-2_eeg.vhdr. Here, run- distinguishes the identical acquisitions within the same session.

A continuous MEG recording is split into parts due to file size limits. The split- entity is used (e.g., split-01, split-02), and if a scans.tsv file is provided, all parts must be listed separately with identical acq_time values.

Continuous physiological signals are recorded alongside EEG. The recording- entity might be used to label different signal types or instruments, such as recording-ECG or recording-contrast, to distinguish them from the primary electrophysiological stream.
common_causes: Uncertainty about when to use run- versus recording- entities for continuous data.
Confusion regarding the optional nature of acquisition and run in the base raw template versus modality-specific requirements.
Attempting to use run- when other entities (like ses- or acq-) already sufficiently distinguish the files.
Improperly renaming split continuous files without updating internal file pointers.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Review the BIDS Entity Table and modality-specific chapters (EEG, MEG, etc.) to confirm which entities are actually required versus optional for your specific data type. Use the run- entity only when multiple recordings share identical acquisition parameters within a session. If different parameters or sessions distinguish the files, run- may be omitted. For continuous files exceeding 2GB, use dedicated tools like MNE-Python to split and rename files, ensuring internal pointers are updated correctly.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: The existing schema marks acquisition and run as optional in the base raw template, but modality-specific rules may impose stricter requirements. The retrieval_text in the original record mentions these as required, which may reflect a specific modality override or a discrepancy; users should always verify against the modality-specific BIDS specification. The recording- entity is distinct from the template name and is used specifically to label continuous streams.

title: Raw File Template: task
summary: Defines filename structure for task raw BIDS files.
retrieval_text: The raw template 'task' defines filename entity requirements. Entities include: task (required)

ai_enrichment.description: The `task` entity is a required component in the filename templates for raw BIDS data files that involve structured activities. It identifies the specific set of structured activities performed by a participant during a data acquisition session. According to the BIDS specification, a task is always tied to one data acquisition, meaning that multiple conceptually different behaviors performed during a single acquisition are grouped into a single combined task.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: In BIDS Manager, the `task` entity serves as a mandatory identifier for raw recording files. When `task` is marked as 'required' in the raw template, it means every raw file associated with a task-based acquisition must include a `task-<label>` component in its filename. The label is typically derived from a task name defined in the dataset's metadata (e.g., `TaskName` in JSON sidecars), with non-alphanumeric characters removed.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Correctly specifying the `task` entity ensures that data is properly grouped and indexed by the activities performed. It is essential for downstream processing pipelines that rely on task labels to route data to the correct analysis streams. It also prevents naming conflicts and ensures compliance with BIDS validation rules.
example_scenarios: A functional MRI dataset includes a memory task named 'Faces N-Back'. The raw BOLD file is named `sub-01_task-facesnback_run-1_bold.nii.gz`. The task label `facesnback` is derived from the task name by removing spaces and non-alphanumeric characters.
A resting-state fMRI scan is treated as a task in BIDS. Following recommended conventions, the task label begins with `rest`, resulting in a filename like `sub-01_task-rest_run-1_bold.nii.gz`.

During a single EEG acquisition, a participant performs both a visual oddball task and an auditory oddball task. Because they occurred in the same acquisition session, they are combined into one task, and all corresponding raw files share the same `task-` label.
common_causes: Missing `task-` label in filenames for task-based recordings.
Using invalid characters (e.g., spaces, hyphens) in the task label.
Assigning different task labels to files acquired during the same continuous recording session.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Verify that all raw files for a given acquisition include a `task-<label>` component. Ensure the label contains only alphanumeric characters and matches the `TaskName` field in the corresponding metadata JSON files. If multiple behaviors were recorded in one session, consolidate them under a single task label.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: The `task` entity is part of the broader `recording` entity group referenced in the raw template. While `task` is required for task-based data, it may be optional or handled differently for certain non-task modalities or resting-state conventions. Resting-state data is explicitly treated as a task in BIDS.

ai_enrichment.description: The 'mri' raw file template defines the standardized naming convention and entity requirements for raw magnetic resonance imaging data within a BIDS dataset. It specifies which entities (such as contrast agent, reconstruction, and chunk) are permitted, their allowed values, and the strict ordering required in filenames.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This template governs how raw MRI files (e.g., anatomical, functional, or diffusion images) are named. The entities listed indicate which metadata dimensions can be used to distinguish files. While the existing record references specific entities, BIDS generally treats entities like 'ce-' (contrast enhancing agent), 'rec-' (reconstruction), and 'chunk-' as optional. They should only be included in filenames when they accurately describe the acquisition or processing characteristics of the file.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Adhering to the 'mri' template ensures consistent and predictable filename structures across the dataset. This consistency is critical for automated validation tools, data sharing platforms, and downstream processing pipelines that parse filenames to extract metadata and organize data correctly.
example_scenarios: A researcher acquires a T1-weighted scan with a contrast agent. To distinguish it from non-contrast scans, they include the 'ce-' entity: sub-01_ce-gadolinium_T1w.nii.gz
A dataset contains multiple reconstructions of the same raw data, such as motion-corrected and uncorrected versions. The 'rec-' entity is used to differentiate them: sub-01_rec-MoCo_T1w.nii.gz
For acquisitions split into multiple segments (e.g., multi-band or chunked acquisitions), the 'chunk-' entity identifies specific parts: sub-01_chunk-1_T1w.nii.gz
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: When organizing raw MRI data, verify that filenames strictly follow the 'mri' template structure. Include optional entities only when relevant to the specific file. Ensure that the order of entities matches the BIDS Entity Table, and that any included entities have corresponding valid values defined in the specification.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: In BIDS filename templates, the '_' placeholder denotes an arbitrary sequence of valid entities and labels. Entities enclosed in square brackets (e.g., [_ses-]) are optional. The ordering of entities is strictly defined and must be followed regardless of whether they are required or optional.

ai_enrichment.description: The 'epi' raw file template defines the naming convention and entity requirements for files using the 'epi' suffix in BIDS. This suffix is primarily used for echo-planar imaging data, which includes BOLD functional scans, fieldmaps, and phase-contrast flow images. The template specifies which filename entities are expected or permitted, serving as a structural guide for consistent dataset organization.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: The provided knowledge record indicates that the schema currently marks 'direction' and 'part' as optional entities for the 'epi' template. However, users should note that the retrieval text references them as required, which may reflect a specific use case (e.g., fieldmap files often require 'direction' to denote phase-encoding). In BIDS, entities enclosed in square brackets in the specification are optional, but modality-specific rules may mandate certain entities depending on the imaging sequence. The template acts as a baseline structure that should be adapted to the actual data type and acquisition parameters.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Adhering to the 'epi' filename template ensures that BIDS-compliant tools, validators, and processing pipelines correctly identify and interpret the data. Incorrect naming or missing required entities can trigger validation errors, hinder automated distortion correction (e.g., for fieldmaps), or cause downstream analysis failures. Consistent application of the template also improves dataset readability and interoperability across research teams.
example_scenarios: A researcher saves a fieldmap as 'sub-01_dir-AP_epi.nii.gz'. The 'dir-AP' entity correctly specifies the phase-encoding direction, which is typically required for susceptibility distortion correction.

A functional scan is named 'sub-01_task-rest_bold.nii.gz'. Since 'direction' is not applicable to standard BOLD acquisitions, its absence aligns with the template's flexibility for non-fieldmap 'epi' data.

A user attempts to name a file 'sub-01_epi.nii.gz' without task or run entities. While structurally valid for a fieldmap, this would be invalid for a functional scan, highlighting the need to match entities to the specific imaging sequence.
common_causes: Confusion between general template definitions and modality-specific requirements (e.g., fieldmaps vs. BOLD scans).
Inconsistent application of entity labels across files within the same dataset.
Relying solely on schema flags without consulting the official BIDS specification for the specific imaging sequence.
Misinterpreting optional entities in the template as universally required or prohibited.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Verify the specific requirements for the 'epi' suffix based on your dataset's content (e.g., is it a fieldmap, BOLD, or phase-contrast scan?). Consult the official BIDS MRI specification to confirm whether 'direction' or other entities are mandatory for your use case. Ensure filenames strictly follow the '<entities>_<suffix>.<ext>' format and that entity values match valid BIDS labels. Cross-reference the schema's 'optional' designation with the actual data acquisition parameters.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: The BIDS specification uses square brackets '[]' to denote optional entities in filename templates. The 'epi' suffix is versatile and used across different MRI sequences, so entity requirements can vary significantly. The existing record contains a discrepancy between the retrieval text (marking 'direction' and 'part' as required) and the raw content (marking them as optional). Users should prioritize the official BIDS specification and validator behavior over schema defaults when curating datasets.

ai_enrichment.description: The raw file template for 'pet' defines the naming convention and entity requirements for Positron Emission Tomography (PET) data stored in the pet/ directory. It specifies which BIDS entities (such as task, tracer, reconstruction, run, and recording) are required or optional depending on the specific file suffix (e.g., _pet, _blood, _events, _physio).
ai_enrichment.interpretation: The existing knowledge record correctly lists task, tracer, reconstruction, and run as optional in the base template. In practice, these entities are optional for most PET file types, but their requirement status depends on the specific suffix. For example, task is required for _events, _physio, and _stim files, while recording is required for _blood files. Users should interpret the template as providing a flexible framework where entity requirements are determined by the exact file type and experimental design, rather than treating all listed entities as mandatory.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Accurately applying entity requirements ensures that PET datasets pass BIDS validation and remain compatible with standard BIDS processing pipelines. Misinterpreting optional entities as required can lead to unnecessary validation errors or forced metadata, while omitting required entities (like task for event files) will cause validation failures and hinder downstream analysis.
example_scenarios: A resting-state PET imaging scan with a specific radiotracer and reconstruction method might be named sub-01_task-rest_trc-FDG_rec-standard_pet.nii.gz, where task, tracer, and reconstruction are present but optional.
Blood sampling data for a specific recording session requires the recording entity: sub-01_ses-01_task-rest_trc-FDG_rec-standard_run-1_recording-1_blood.tsv.
An event file for a task-based PET study requires the task entity: sub-01_task-language_trc-FDG_events.tsv.
common_causes: Assuming all entities listed in a template are mandatory for every file type.
Confusing PET file suffixes and their specific entity requirements.
Inconsistent labeling of tasks or tracers across subjects and sessions.
Omitting the recording entity for blood data files.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Consult the BIDS specification's entity table for PET to determine which entities are required for your specific file suffix. Ensure that if task is used, it is consistently applied across all subjects and sessions. For blood data, verify that the recording- entity is present. Use the BIDS Validator to identify and correct entity-related naming errors.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: The pet/ directory is designated for raw PET data, while imaging data may also be stored as 4D (or 3D) NIfTI files. 'Rest' is considered a valid task label in BIDS. The existing retrieval text may suggest certain entities are required, but the official specification clarifies that task, tracer, reconstruction, and run are optional for the base template, with requirements varying by suffix.

ai_enrichment.description: The BIDS specification defines a filename template for raw Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy (MRS) data files. The template follows the standard BIDS pattern: sub-<label>[_ses-<label>][_task-<label>][_acq-<label>][_nuc-<label>][_voi-<label>][_rec-<label>][_run-<index>][_echo-<index>][_inv-<index>]_<suffix>.<extension>. Entities enclosed in square brackets are optional by default.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: The existing record contains a contradiction: the retrieval_text claims task, nucleus, volume, and reconstruction are required, while the raw_content correctly lists them as optional. According to the official BIDS specification and the MRS-BIDS extension, these entities are optional. They should only be included when necessary to differentiate between multiple acquisitions within the same subject and session. Users should use the minimum number of entities required to make filenames unique.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Correctly applying optional versus required entities prevents validation errors and ensures downstream tools parse the dataset accurately. Over-specifying entities creates unnecessarily long filenames, while under-specifying them can cause ambiguity when multiple scans exist in the same directory.
example_scenarios: A proton MRS scan from subject 01, session 02, performing an n-back task with a semi-LASER sequence targeting the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex: sub-01_ses-02_task-nback_acq-slaser_nuc-1H_voi-dlpfc_svs.nii.gz
A basic MRS reference file with only mandatory identifiers: sub-01_mrsref.json
common_causes: Misinterpreting MRS-BIDS guidelines that state entities are required only for disambiguation.
Confusion between core BIDS requirements and extension-specific optional entities.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Verify that every entity in the filename is necessary to distinguish the file from others in the same directory. If a file is unique without certain entities, omit task-, nuc-, voi-, or rec-. Ensure filenames follow the template order and use valid MRS suffixes (svs, mrsi, mrsref, unloc).
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: MRS data must be stored in the mrs/ subdirectory. The MRS-BIDS specification is a BIDS Extension Proposal (BEP). Valid suffixes for raw MRS files include svs (single-voxel spectroscopy), mrsi (MRS imaging), mrsref (MRS reference scan), and unloc (unlocalized signal).

title: Derivative Template: base
summary: Defines filename structure, extensions, and suffixes for base derivatives.
retrieval_text: The derivative template 'base' defines filename structure. Entities: subject, session, description. Extensions: various.

ai_enrichment.description: The 'base' derivative template defines the standard filename structure for files within a BIDS Derivatives dataset. According to the BIDS specification, derivative filenames must follow the pattern `<source_entities>[_keyword-<value>]_<suffix>.<ext>`, where `<source_entities>` are inherited from the raw source file (excluding its original suffix and extension). The template specifies that the `subject` and `session` entities are optional (though typically inherited to maintain provenance), and the `description` entity (often represented as `desc-`) is also optional, used to label the processing step or specific characteristic of the derivative.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: For a BIDS Manager user, this record indicates that when a dataset is identified as a derivative (via `DatasetType: 'derivative'` in `dataset_description.json`), the validator will apply this template to check derivative filenames. It means derivative files should retain the subject and session identifiers from their raw counterparts, and may optionally include a `desc` entity to clarify the nature of the processed data. The template does not enforce a specific suffix or extension, allowing flexibility for various derivative types (e.g., NIfTI, JSON, TSV).
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Adhering to this template ensures that derivative files are correctly linked to their raw source data, which is critical for reproducibility and data provenance. It also prevents naming conflicts with permissible raw BIDS filenames, as derivatives must use modified filenames that do not match raw data patterns. Proper use of the `desc` entity helps users and software distinguish between different processing stages or variations of the same data type.
example_scenarios: A preprocessed T1-weighted image derived from a raw scan: `sub-01_ses-01_desc-preproc_T1w.nii.gz`. Here, `sub-01` and `ses-01` are inherited from the raw file, and `desc-preproc` indicates the processing step.
A group-level statistical map without subject/session specificity: `desc-group_stat_zstat.nii.gz`. The subject and session entities are omitted as the file is not subject- or session-specific.
A sidecar JSON file describing derivative metadata: `sub-01_ses-01_desc-preproc_T1w.json`. Follows the same entity chain as its corresponding NIfTI file.
common_causes: This template is automatically applied by the BIDS Validator when `dataset_description.json` contains `"DatasetType": "derivative"`.
It is relevant whenever organizing, renaming, or validating files within a derivatives directory.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: When validating a derivatives dataset, ensure that derivative filenames start with the source entities (e.g., `sub-`, `ses-`) and use a valid derivative suffix. If using the `desc` entity, verify that the corresponding `descriptions.tsv` file (if present) accurately documents the labels used. Ensure no derivative filename matches a permissible raw BIDS filename unless it is an identical copy.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: Every derivatives dataset is considered a BIDS dataset and must include a `dataset_description.json` file at the root level. Files should be organized into subject and session directories mirroring the raw dataset structure. The `desc` entity is highly recommended for documenting how files are generated, though its use alongside a `descriptions.tsv` file may not guarantee full computational reproducibility.

retrieval_text: The derivative template 'spatial' defines filename structure. Entities: space. Extensions: various.

ai_enrichment.description: The 'spatial' derivative template defines the filename structure for derivatives that have been aligned to a specific spatial reference. It primarily utilizes the `space` entity to indicate the coordinate system or template to which the data has been registered.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: In BIDS Derivatives, the `space` entity is optional but highly recommended for distinguishing files aligned to different coordinate systems or reference maps. When the `space` entity is omitted, or when its value is not listed in the Standard template identifiers, the `SpatialReference` metadata field becomes REQUIRED in the accompanying JSON sidecar. This ensures that the spatial alignment of the derivative is explicitly documented.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Properly specifying the spatial reference is essential for downstream analyses, as it allows researchers to compare data across runs, sessions, subjects, or datasets. It guarantees that the spatial context of processed images is unambiguous, which is critical for reproducibility and accurate interpretation of results.
example_scenarios: A preprocessed T1-weighted image aligned to MNI152NLin2009cAsym would be named `sub-01_space-MNI152NLin2009cAsym_desc-preproc_T1w.nii.gz`.

If a derivative is aligned to a custom, non-standard space not listed in the BIDS standard template identifiers, the `space` entity may be omitted or set to a custom label, but the `SpatialReference` metadata MUST be provided in the JSON file to point to the reference image (e.g., a URI or path relative to the dataset root).
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: When organizing derivative files, include the `space` entity in the filename if the data is aligned to a recognized standard template. If using a custom space or omitting the entity, ensure the `SpatialReference` metadata is added to the JSON sidecar. Verify that the `space` value corresponds to a valid Image-Based Coordinate System or is clearly defined in the metadata.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: The spatial template does not introduce new suffixes or extensions; it permits any valid BIDS/BIDS Derivatives filename. The `space` entity values are drawn from the Image-Based Coordinate Systems specification. Note that the specification for spatial transforms (BEP 014) is under development, so transform file specifications may evolve.

title: Derivative Template: volumetric
summary: Defines filename structure, extensions, and suffixes for volumetric derivatives.
retrieval_text: The derivative template 'volumetric' defines filename structure. Entities: resolution. Extensions: .nii.gz, .nii, .json.

ai_enrichment.description: The 'volumetric' derivative template defines the filename structure, allowed extensions, and applicable entities for volumetric derivative data in BIDS. It is designed for preprocessed, coregistered, or resampled 3D/4D regularly sampled images. The template specifies .nii.gz, .nii, and .json as valid extensions and highlights the resolution (res) entity as an optional component.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: When organizing volumetric derivatives, filenames must follow the standard BIDS pattern: [<source-entities>_]<entity-value>_<suffix>.<extension>. The resolution entity is optional but derivative-specific. If the res- entity is included in a filename, the corresponding Resolution metadata field MUST be present in the sidecar JSON file to define the interpretation of that resolution value. BIDS strictly enforces that data files are uniquely identified by their entities, datatype, and suffix; therefore, only one file per unique combination is permitted, even if multiple extensions are allowed. Metadata files (JSON) are exempt from this uniqueness rule.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Adhering to this template ensures that derivative datasets are machine-readable, consistently organized, and pass BIDS validation. Proper use of the resolution entity and its associated metadata prevents ambiguity when multiple versions of the same derivative exist at different resolutions. Strict uniqueness rules prevent file conflicts that could break downstream processing pipelines or cause validator errors.
example_scenarios: A researcher provides a preprocessed T1-weighted volume at native resolution. The file is named sub-01_ses-01_desc-preproc_T1w.nii.gz, and the sidecar JSON includes the field Resolution: native.

To avoid naming conflicts, the same derivative is provided at two different resolutions. The files are named sub-01_ses-01_res-1mm_desc-preproc_T1w.nii.gz and sub-01_ses-01_res-2mm_desc-preproc_T1w.nii.gz, each with a corresponding Resolution metadata entry.

A dataset incorrectly contains both sub-01_ses-01_desc-preproc_T1w.nii and sub-01_ses-01_desc-preproc_T1w.nii.gz. BIDS validation will flag this as a conflict because data files must be uniquely identified by entities, datatype, and suffix.
common_causes: Omitting the Resolution metadata field when the res- entity is used in a derivative filename.
Creating duplicate data files with different extensions (e.g., .nii and .nii.gz) for the same entities and suffix.
Applying the resolution entity to raw (non-derivative) data, as it is exclusively for derivative datasets.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Verify that any derivative filename containing the res- entity has a corresponding Resolution field in its JSON sidecar. If multiple files share the same entities, datatype, and suffix but differ only by extension, retain only one version (preferably .nii.gz as recommended by the specification). Ensure the resolution entity is not used in raw data directories, as it is derivative-specific.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: This template references the broader spatial derivative template family (meta.templates.deriv.spatial). The resolution entity is exclusively for regularly sampled N-dimensional data in derivatives. While .nii and .nii.gz are both permitted, the BIDS specification strongly recommends compressed NIfTI files. Metadata files are exempt from the uniqueness rule and should accompany each data file.

title: Derivative Template: surface
summary: Defines filename structure, extensions, and suffixes for surface derivatives.
retrieval_text: The derivative template 'surface' defines filename structure. Entities: hemisphere, density. Extensions: various.

ai_enrichment.description: The "surface" derivative template defines the standardized filename structure, required entities, and file extensions for surface-based outputs in BIDS Derivatives datasets. It primarily governs GIFTI and CIFTI-2 file naming conventions, specifying how to encode hemisphere information, surface sampling density, and data intent (e.g., geometry, functional time series, or parcellations).
ai_enrichment.interpretation: When working with surface derivatives, this template indicates that files should follow GIFTI naming conventions with intent-specific extensions (such as .surf.gii for geometry or .label.gii for parcellations). The hemi- entity is mandatory for files representing a single hemisphere, and the den- entity is used to denote surface mesh density. If den- is used, the accompanying JSON metadata must include a "Density" field to define the sampling scheme.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Adhering to this template ensures that surface derivatives are correctly identified and processed by BIDS-compliant software. It prevents naming conflicts when multiple surface densities or resolutions are present, guarantees that critical spatial metadata (like vertex density) is explicitly documented, and maintains compatibility with neuroimaging pipelines that rely on standardized surface file structures.
example_scenarios: A researcher generates a left-hemisphere cortical parcellation. The file is saved as sub-01_task-rest_hemi-L_den-41k_dseg.label.gii, with a JSON sidecar defining the "Density" metadata for the 41k vertex mesh.

A processing pipeline outputs surface-based fMRI time series for both hemispheres. The files use the .func.gii extension and include the hemi- entity (e.g., hemi-R_func.gii), ensuring hemibrain-specific data is correctly labeled.

A dataset contains derivatives at multiple surface sampling densities. The den- entity is used to distinguish them (e.g., den-10k vs den-41k), avoiding filename collisions and allowing tools to automatically select the appropriate resolution.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Verify that all surface derivative files use intent-specific GIFTI extensions (e.g., .label.gii, .func.gii) rather than bare .gii files. Ensure the hemi- entity is present for hemibrain-restricted data. If the den- entity is included in the filename, confirm that the corresponding JSON metadata contains a "Density" field with a valid definition.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: The den- entity is exclusively applicable to derivative data and represents the density of non-parametric surfaces. It corresponds to the "Density" metadata field. While res- and den- can coexist, they are only permitted together in files that combine regularly sampled (volume) and surface-sampled data. Discrete surface segmentations must strictly use .label.gii (GIFTI) or .dlabel.nii (CIFTI-2).

title: Derivative Template: mask
summary: Defines filename structure, extensions, and suffixes for mask derivatives.
retrieval_text: The derivative template 'mask' defines filename structure. Entities: label. Extensions: various. Suffixes: mask.

ai_enrichment.description: The `mask` suffix designates a binary mask file in BIDS-Derivatives that functions as a discrete label for a single structure. It represents a 3D volume where voxels inside the region of interest are typically assigned a value of 1 and those outside are 0. This suffix is exclusively reserved for derivative datasets and should not be used for raw data.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: When a file uses the `_mask` suffix, it indicates a binary segmentation rather than a continuous or probabilistic map. The filename must include the `space` entity to explicitly define the coordinate system. If the mask corresponds to a specific anatomical structure derived from an atlas, the `label` entity should be used to identify the structure, and the `Atlas` metadata field should be defined in the accompanying JSON file to link it to its source.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Correctly applying the `mask` suffix and associated entities ensures that analysis pipelines and visualization tools interpret the file as a binary region-of-interest (ROI) mask. Explicitly stating the `space` entity prevents coordinate system ambiguity, which is critical for accurate image registration and spatial analysis. Using `label` and `Atlas` metadata avoids confusion when multiple structures or atlases are processed simultaneously.
example_scenarios: A researcher creates a binary mask for the left hippocampus using an MNI152 template. The file is named `sub-01_space-MNI152NLin6Asym_label-LHippocampus_mask.nii.gz` and includes an `Atlas` metadata field pointing to the MNI152 template.

A skull-stripped brain mask is generated in native subject space without any spatial transformation. It is named `sub-01_ses-01_space-orig_mask.nii.gz`, adhering to the recommendation to use `space-orig` when no transformation is applied.

A tumor segmentation is converted into a binary mask for a specific subject's T1-weighted image. The filename uses `label-Tumor` and `space-T1w` to clearly indicate the structure and the native coordinate system.
common_causes: Confusing binary masks (`_mask`) with continuous or probabilistic segmentations (`_seg`), which serve different analytical purposes.
Omitting the required `space` entity, leaving downstream tools unable to determine the coordinate system.
Attempting to use the `_mask` suffix in raw BIDS datasets, where it is not permitted.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Verify that the file resides in a derivatives directory and uses the `_mask` suffix. Ensure the `space` entity is present in the filename to define the coordinate system. If the mask represents a specific structure from an atlas, add the `label` entity and define the `Atlas` metadata in the JSON sidecar. Confirm that the image data contains only binary values (0 and 1) rather than continuous probabilities.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: The `mask` suffix is strictly for binary masks. For multi-class tissue segmentations or probabilistic maps, the `_seg` suffix should be used instead. The `space` entity is mandatory to disambiguate derivatives across different coordinate systems. If no spatial transformation has been applied, `space-orig` is the recommended value.

retrieval_text: The derivative template 'dseg' defines filename structure. Entities: atlas, segmentation, scale. Extensions: .nii.gz, .nii, .tsv, .json. Suffixes: dseg.

ai_enrichment.description: The 'dseg' template defines the filename structure, extensions, and suffixes for discrete segmentation derivative files. The suffix 'dseg' stands for 'Discrete Segmentation' and is exclusively reserved for derivative datasets. It supports image formats (.nii.gz, .nii) and tabular/metadata formats (.tsv, .json).
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This template is primarily used for atlas-based segmentation results. According to the BIDS Derivatives specification, files using this template must include the 'space-' entity to specify the coordinate system, and the 'atlas-' entity to identify the source atlas. Additional entities like 'seg-' and 'scale-' are conditionally required when disambiguating multiple realizations or resolutions of the same atlas. The accompanying '.tsv' file defines the label mapping (e.g., index, name, abbreviation, color, mapping) for the integer values in the segmentation image.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Proper use of the 'dseg' template ensures that segmentation derivatives are correctly organized, spatially referenced, and accompanied by clear label definitions. This is critical for downstream analysis, reproducibility, and validation, especially when multiple atlases, segmentations, or scales are involved.
example_scenarios: A subject-level segmentation derived from the Schaefer 2018 atlas at a 100-region scale: sub-01_atlas-Schaefer2018_seg-7n_scale-100_space-MNI152NLin2009cAsym_dseg.nii.gz

The corresponding metadata file sub-01_atlas-Schaefer2018_seg-7n_scale-100_space-MNI152NLin2009cAsym_dseg.tsv containing columns for index, name, and color to map integer values in the segmentation image to anatomical regions.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: When creating or validating 'dseg' files, ensure that the filename includes the 'space-' and 'atlas-' entities. If the atlas has multiple segmentations or scales, include 'seg-' and/or 'scale-' accordingly. Provide a companion '.tsv' file that defines the semantic meaning of each integer label in the segmentation image, following the standard BIDS label table format.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: The 'dseg' template inherits from the volumetric derivative template. While 'space-' and 'atlas-' are required, 'seg-' and 'scale-' are conditionally required based on the atlas characteristics. TSV files defining labels are typically placed in the root of the derivatives hierarchy or alongside the image files, following common BIDS principles.

title: Derivative Template: probseg
summary: Defines filename structure, extensions, and suffixes for probseg derivatives.
retrieval_text: The derivative template 'probseg' defines filename structure. Entities: atlas, segmentation, scale, label. Extensions: .nii.gz, .nii, .json. Suffixes: probseg.

ai_enrichment.description: The probseg suffix designates a probabilistic segmentation file within a BIDS Derivatives dataset. Unlike discrete segmentations (dseg), probabilistic segmentations represent the likelihood of a voxel belonging to a specific label or region, often resulting from atlas-based parcellation or tissue classification. This suffix is exclusively permitted in derivative datasets.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: The probseg template defines the naming convention for these files, supporting entities such as space-, atlas-, seg-, scale-, and label-. These entities are crucial for disambiguating the spatial coordinate system (space-), the source atlas (atlas-), different realizations of the same atlas (seg-), varying resolutions or scales (scale-), and specific anatomical labels (label-). While these entities are optional in the template definition, the BIDS specification requires space- and atlas- to disambiguate derivatives defined with respect to different coordinate systems or atlas versions. A corresponding .json sidecar is required to describe the label map or probabilistic values.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Proper use of the probseg template ensures that atlas-derived data is correctly contextualized. Since probabilistic maps can vary significantly based on the reference space, atlas version, and processing scale, explicitly encoding these attributes in the filename prevents confusion during downstream analysis and validation. It also distinguishes probabilistic outputs from discrete segmentations or masks.
example_scenarios: A probabilistic segmentation of a subject's brain mapped to MNI152NLin2009cAsym space using the AAL atlas: sub-01_space-MNI152NLin2009cAsym_atlas-AAL_probseg.nii.gz

A probabilistic map of spinal cord structures derived from the PAM50 template, with a specific label identifying a single tract: sub-01_space-PAM50_atlas-PAM50_label-WM_left_lateral_reticulospinal_tract_probseg.nii.gz
A probabilistic segmentation at a specific scale (e.g., 1mm resolution) to disambiguate from coarser versions: sub-01_space-T1w_atlas-IXI_scale-1mm_probseg.nii.gz
common_causes: Attempting to use the probseg suffix in a raw BIDS dataset, as it is derivative-only.
Omitting required disambiguating entities like space- or atlas- when multiple coordinate systems or atlases are used.
Failing to provide a .json sidecar to define the LabelMap or probabilistic nature of the data.
Confusing probseg with dseg (discrete segmentation) or mask suffixes.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Verify the file is located within a BIDS Derivatives directory structure. Ensure the filename includes the space- entity to specify the coordinate system and the atlas- entity if derived from a specific atlas. Include the seg- or scale- entities if the atlas has multiple realizations or resolutions that need disambiguation. Use the label- entity to identify specific structures when storing one structure per file. Provide a companion .json sidecar file containing metadata such as LabelMap to describe the probabilistic values or labels.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: The probseg suffix is distinct from dseg and mask. When using the label- entity, it identifies a specific structure within the probabilistic map, which is useful when storing one structure per file. The scale- entity is particularly relevant for atlases that provide data at multiple resolutions or 'brain unit' definitions. The .json sidecar is essential for encoding atlas-derived results and should follow the prescriptions of the Common image-derived labels section.

title: Derivative Template: dseg_surface
summary: Defines filename structure, extensions, and suffixes for dseg_surface derivatives.
retrieval_text: The derivative template 'dseg_surface' defines filename structure. Entities: atlas, segmentation, scale. Extensions: .label.gii, .dlabel.nii, .tsv, .json. Suffixes: dseg.

ai_enrichment.description: The `dseg_surface` template defines the naming conventions and file structures for discrete surface-based segmentations and parcellations derived from atlases. It specifies valid extensions (`.label.gii`, `.dlabel.nii`, `.tsv`, `.json`) and the `dseg` suffix. These files represent spatial annotations, such as anatomical landmarks, segmentations, or parcellations, typically defined on a surface coordinate system.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: While the base record lists `atlas-`, `seg-`, and `scale-` as optional, the BIDS specification clarifies that `atlas-` is REQUIRED for files derived from a specific atlas. The `seg-` entity is REQUIRED when an atlas has multiple realizations (e.g., different parcellation criteria), and `scale-` is REQUIRED to distinguish different regional resolutions (e.g., number of ROIs). Additionally, `space-` is generally REQUIRED for derivatives to specify the coordinate system. The `dseg.tsv` metadata file is typically placed in the root of the derivatives dataset hierarchy rather than inside a modality folder.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Correctly applying these entities and extensions ensures that surface-based segmentation files are unambiguously identified and validated. It allows downstream tools to correctly interpret the atlas source, segmentation criteria, and regional resolution. Using derivative-only extensions like `.dlabel.nii` or `.label.gii` prevents confusion with raw anatomical data and ensures compliance with BIDS-Derivatives validation rules.
example_scenarios: A user generates a surface parcellation using the Schaefer 2018 atlas with 100 regions. The correct filename would be `sub-01_atlas-Schaefer2018_seg-100_scale-100_dseg.tsv` (placed in the derivatives root) and `sub-01_atlas-Schaefer2018_seg-100_scale-100_dseg.label.gii` (in the appropriate surface directory).

A pipeline produces two different segmentations from the same atlas (e.g., 7-network and 17-network versions). The `seg-` entity must be used to disambiguate them: `sub-01_atlas-Schaefer2018_seg-7n_dseg.tsv` and `sub-01_atlas-Schaefer2018_seg-17n_dseg.tsv`.

A validator flags a missing `atlas-` entity on a file named `sub-01_scale-100_dseg.label.gii`. This occurs because the file is derived from an atlas, making the `atlas-` entity mandatory per BIDS-Derivatives rules.
common_causes: Omitting the `atlas-` entity when the segmentation is derived from a known atlas.
Using raw-data extensions (like `.nii.gz`) instead of derivative-specific ones (`.dlabel.nii`, `.label.gii`).
Placing `dseg.tsv` files inside modality directories instead of the derivatives root.
Failing to include `seg-` or `scale-` when multiple resolutions or realizations of the same atlas exist.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Review the filename to ensure the `atlas-` entity is included, as it is required for atlas-derived files. If multiple realizations or resolutions exist, verify that `seg-` and `scale-` are used appropriately. Confirm that the file extension matches one of the supported derivative formats (`.label.gii`, `.dlabel.nii`, `.tsv`, `.json`). Check that accompanying `dseg.tsv` files are located in the derivatives root directory.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: The `dseg` suffix and extensions like `.dlabel.nii` and `.label.gii` are exclusively for derivative datasets. The `scale-` entity specifically refers to regional resolution, often indicated by the number of regions of interest (ROIs). Surface-based segmentations often accompany CIFTI-2 dense label files (`.dlabel.nii`) or Gifti label files (`.label.gii`).

title: Derivative Template: surface_map
summary: Defines filename structure, extensions, and suffixes for surface_map derivatives.
retrieval_text: The derivative template 'surface_map' defines filename structure. Entities: . Extensions: .func.gii, .json.

ai_enrichment.description: The 'surface_map' derivative template defines the naming conventions, extensions, and metadata requirements for functional data that has been projected from volume space onto a surface mesh. It specifies that functional surface data should use the '.func.gii' GIFTI extension, which indicates functional intent, and must be accompanied by a '.json' sidecar file for metadata.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: When working with surface-mapped functional derivatives, this template indicates that the data represents either time series or statistical maps mapped to cortical vertices. The '.func.gii' extension is mandatory for functional intent in GIFTI files, replacing the use of bare '.gii' extensions. The accompanying '.json' file is required to store metadata, such as column descriptions for time series or details about statistical maps. Suffixes typically follow the 'map' convention (e.g., 'boldmap', 'cbvmap') or reflect specific algorithmic outputs.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Adhering to this template ensures that surface functional derivatives are correctly distinguished from raw volume data and other derivative types. It guarantees that neuroimaging tools and BIDS validators can properly interpret the file format and intent. The mandatory '.json' sidecar preserves critical metadata needed for downstream analysis, such as column names for spatiotemporal decompositions or statistical map parameters.
example_scenarios: A researcher projects task-related activation maps from a volume-based fMRI analysis onto a subject's cortical surface. The resulting files follow the template, e.g., 'sub-01_task-rest_space-fsaverage_boldmap.func.gii' with a corresponding '.json' sidecar containing map metadata.

A spatiotemporal decomposition algorithm (like ICA) outputs spatial component maps on a surface. These are saved as 'sub-01_task-rest_space-fsaverage_ICA1.func.gii' with a data dictionary JSON file describing the columns, as required for decomposition outputs.
A user incorrectly names a surface functional file with a bare '.gii' extension instead of '.func.gii', triggering a BIDS validation warning about non-standard extensions for GIFTI files.
common_causes: Using a bare '.gii' extension instead of the intent-specific '.func.gii' extension.
Omitting the required '.json' sidecar file for metadata storage.
Applying volume-based suffixes without appending the 'map' suffix for derivative outputs.
Failing to include necessary metadata fields in the sidecar JSON, such as column descriptions for time series data.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Verify that surface functional derivatives use the '.func.gii' extension rather than a bare '.gii'. Ensure a corresponding '.json' sidecar file is present and contains appropriate metadata (e.g., column names for time series or statistical map details). Confirm that the suffix follows BIDS conventions for derivative maps, typically by appending 'map' to the original suffix (e.g., 'bold' becomes 'boldmap'). If multiple derivatives differ only by surface sampling density, use the 'den-' entity to avoid naming conflicts.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: GIFTI files are XML-based and well-suited for describing surface geometry and parcellations. The '.func.gii' extension specifically denotes functional intent according to the GIFTI specification. When files represent spatial time series, the '.json' sidecar must describe the data structure. If a derivatives chain involves outputs derived from a single raw input, 'source-entities' must be included in the filename.

title: Atlas Template: base
summary: Defines filename entity requirements for atlas files: template, cohort, atlas.
retrieval_text: The atlas template 'base' specifies entity requirements for atlas BIDS files. Required/allowed entities include: template, cohort, atlas.

ai_enrichment.description: The base atlas template defines the standard filename entity structure for BIDS-compliant atlas and derivative files. It requires the template entity (tpl-) to identify the spatial reference framework, while allowing the optional cohort entity (cohort-) to distinguish between multiple subject groups aggregated into the same template, and the optional atlas entity (atlas-) to specify the particular neuroanatomical or functional annotation scheme.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: In BIDS, template files replace subject-level (sub-) directories and entities. The tpl- entity is mandatory for these files to establish the common spatial coordinate frame. The cohort- entity should be used when a single template aggregates data from several distinct subject groups, acting analogously to the session entity. The atlas- entity identifies the specific labeling or parcellation scheme applied. Together, these entities ensure that spatial derivatives and atlas data are unambiguously linked to their reference spaces and annotation sources.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Correctly applying these entities prevents validation errors and ensures that analysis software can accurately resolve spatial transformations, distinguish between individual subject data and aggregated template data, and correctly map derived annotations to their source atlases. Misusing or omitting these entities can lead to ambiguous file routing, incorrect spatial referencing, and failed validator checks.
example_scenarios: A derivative segmentation file referencing a standard template and a specific atlas: tpl-MNI152NLin2009cAsym_atlas-Schaefer2018_dseg.tsv
A multi-cohort infant template with an atlas label: tpl-MNIInfant_cohort-1_atlas-BrainParc_seg-7n.nii.gz
A single-cohort template instantiation where only the template entity is needed: tpl-MNI152NLin2009cAsym_desc-preproc.nii.gz
common_causes: Confusing subject-level data (sub-) with aggregated template data (tpl-).
Omitting the tpl- entity when files are stored in template directories.
Incorrectly using cohort- when only a single subject group is represented.
Failing to pair atlas- with tpl- when describing derived atlas data.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Verify that all files in template directories use the tpl- entity instead of sub-. Add the cohort- entity only if the template aggregates multiple distinct subject groups. Include the atlas- entity to explicitly name the annotation scheme when files are derived from or represent a specific atlas. Run the BIDS Validator to confirm entity compliance and check the dataset's dataset_description.json for declared spaces and atlases.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: The tpl- and sub- entities are mutually exclusive within a given file. The cohort- entity is structurally analogous to ses- and may appear as both a directory and a filename entity. While the + convention (e.g., MNIInfant+2) exists for spaces, the cohort- entity provides a more explicit and queryable alternative for multi-cohort templates. Derivatives may also require additional entities like space-, seg-, or scale- depending on the analysis pipeline.

ai_enrichment.description: In BIDS, an *atlas* refers to structured neuroanatomical or neurofunctional information expressed as spatial annotations. This includes anatomical landmarks, segmentations, parcellations, probabilistic maps, or feature maps. Atlases are typically defined in relation to a *space* engendered by a specific *template*. Within the BIDS ecosystem, atlases provide standardized, spatially-organized reference data used to label, localize, and interpret imaging features across subjects or studies.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: Users should understand that atlases in BIDS serve as external reference frameworks rather than primary subject-level data. They are primarily organized and referenced within BIDS-Derivatives. When an atlas is used to generate derivatives, the `atlas-` entity is employed to explicitly identify the source atlas. Atlases inherently depend on a coordinate system established by a template (referenced via the `tpl-` entity), which defines the spatial frame of reference for the annotations.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Properly defining and referencing atlases ensures spatial consistency and reproducibility across neuroimaging analyses. It allows downstream tools and validators to correctly interpret segmentation masks, parcellation maps, or probabilistic labels by linking them to their exact source atlas and coordinate space. It also standardizes the distribution of reference data alongside processed derivatives.
example_scenarios: A researcher generates a brain segmentation for a single subject using the Automated Anatomical Labeling (AAL) atlas. The derivative file is named `sub-01_space-MNI152_atlas-AAL_dseg.nii.gz`, where `atlas-AAL` explicitly identifies the reference atlas used.

A study distributes a custom parcellation atlas derived from multiple subjects. The template file `tpl-MyStudy_space-MNI152_dseg.nii.gz` serves as the spatial reference, and the atlas is referenced in downstream derivatives using the `atlas-` entity.

An atlas is distributed with a corresponding lookup table file (e.g., `atlas-AAL_dseg.tsv`) that maps integer values in the segmentation image to anatomical region names, ensuring that downstream matrix or statistical analyses can correctly interpret the labels.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: This record defines a core BIDS concept rather than a validation rule or error. No resolution is required. When organizing atlas-related derivatives, ensure that the `atlas-` entity correctly matches the intended reference atlas, and that the associated `space-` or `tpl-` entities accurately reflect the coordinate system used.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: Atlases in BIDS are closely related to *templates* and *spaces*. While templates establish the spatial coordinate frame (often using the `tpl-` entity), atlases provide the actual anatomical or functional annotations within that frame. The `atlas-` entity is typically used in derivatives. Atlases may also utilize additional entities like `seg-` (to disambiguate different realizations like segmentations vs. parcellations) or `scale-` (for different resolutions or region counts). Reference data is often accompanied by tabular sidecars (`dseg.tsv`) or JSON metadata to define label mappings.

summary:
A continuous uninterrupted block of time during which a brain scanning instrument
or an electromyography recording device was acquiring data
according to a particular scanning sequence/protocol.
retrieval_text:
In BIDS, Data acquisition refers to: A continuous uninterrupted block of time during which a brain scanning instrument
or an electromyography recording device was acquiring data
according to a particular scanning sequence/protocol.
.

raw_content.description:
A continuous uninterrupted block of time during which a brain scanning instrument
or an electromyography recording device was acquiring data
according to a particular scanning sequence/protocol.

ai_enrichment.description: In BIDS, a data acquisition refers to a continuous, uninterrupted block of time during which a brain scanning instrument or an electromyography recording device collects data using a specific scanning sequence or protocol. It represents the fundamental unit of data collection for a participant.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: Users should understand that in BIDS terminology, 'data acquisition' is effectively synonymous with a 'run'. Each acquisition corresponds to a single repetition of data collection that shares the same acquisition parameters and task. While the definition emphasizes 'uninterrupted' time, the practical interpretation of continuity depends on the imaging modality. For instance, in MRI or MEG, the subject must remain in the scanner for the acquisition to remain uninterrupted, whereas certain PET protocols allow the subject to leave and return without breaking the acquisition.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Correctly identifying data acquisitions is essential for proper dataset organization and validation. Each acquisition typically maps to a separate file or set of files labeled with the `run` entity (e.g., `sub-01_task-rest_run-01_bold.nii.gz`). It also dictates how metadata is structured, as a single `TaskName` applies to the entire acquisition, and event tables are organized relative to the start of that acquisition.
example_scenarios: An fMRI experiment where a participant completes a 6-minute resting-state scan without leaving the scanner. This constitutes one data acquisition (one run).

A PET scan where the participant briefly steps out of the scanner room for a bathroom break but the scanner remains active and the acquisition is not restarted. According to BIDS, this still counts as a single uninterrupted data acquisition.

A task-based fMRI study where a participant performs three different cognitive tasks back-to-back without the scanner stopping. This is considered one data acquisition with a combined task, rather than three separate acquisitions.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: When organizing data, group all files belonging to the same uninterrupted collection period under a single `run` index. Ensure that the `TaskName` metadata remains consistent across all files within that acquisition, and use the `run` entity in filenames to distinguish between multiple acquisitions. Verify modality-specific rules to determine whether a break in subject presence actually interrupts the acquisition.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: The BIDS specification explicitly notes that the concept of 'uninterrupted' varies by modality due to the nature of the recording. Additionally, if a subject performs multiple conceptually different behaviors during one continuous scan, BIDS treats it as a single combined task for that acquisition. Events can still change from run to run due to different subject responses or the randomized nature of stimuli, even though the acquisition parameters and task remain the same.

ai_enrichment.description: In BIDS, a data type refers to a functional group of different types of data. Each data type corresponds to a specific directory name (e.g., func, anat, dwi) where files of that modality are stored. This directory structure is nested inside subject and session directories for subject-specific data, while aggregated data like phenotype resides at the dataset root.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: Users should understand that the data type directory is a fundamental organizational unit in BIDS. It dictates how files are grouped and ensures that software tools can automatically locate and process specific modalities without manual configuration. The list of supported data types has evolved across BIDS versions to accommodate new imaging and non-imaging modalities.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Properly assigning files to their correct data type directories is critical for dataset validation, interoperability, and automated processing. Misplaced files or incorrect directory names will cause BIDS validators to flag errors and may prevent analysis pipelines from discovering the data.
example_scenarios: A T1-weighted structural scan is correctly placed in sub-01/anat/sub-01_T1w.nii.gz.
Resting-state fMRI data is stored in sub-01/func/sub-01_task-rest_bold.nii.gz.
Demographic survey data is placed in phenotype/sub-01_demographics.tsv at the dataset root, as phenotype data is aggregated across subjects.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: This is a foundational structural concept rather than a validation error. Users should ensure their dataset structure aligns with the BIDS specification's directory naming conventions for the modalities they are using.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: The BIDS specification has expanded the number of defined data types over time. Early versions (e.g., v1.1.2) defined five types, while later versions (e.g., v1.5.0 and v1.11.x) have added types such as perf, pet, micr, nirs, motion, mrs, phenotype, and emg to support a wider range of neuroimaging and behavioral data.

title: BIDS Concept: Dataset
summary:
A set of neuroimaging and behavioral data acquired for a purpose of a particular study.
A dataset consists of data acquired from one or more subjects, possibly from multiple sessions.
retrieval_text:
In BIDS, Dataset refers to: A set of neuroimaging and behavioral data acquired for a purpose of a particular study.
A dataset consists of data acquired from one or more subjects, possibly from multiple sessions.
.

raw_content.description:
A set of neuroimaging and behavioral data acquired for a purpose of a particular study.
A dataset consists of data acquired from one or more subjects, possibly from multiple sessions.

ai_enrichment.description: In the Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS), a dataset refers to the complete collection of neuroimaging and behavioral data acquired for a specific research study. It serves as the top-level organizational unit, encompassing all data from one or more subjects, and potentially spanning multiple sessions per subject. The dataset acts as the container for all related files, metadata, and documentation required to describe and validate the study's data.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: For a BIDS Manager user, understanding the concept of a dataset is fundamental to navigating and validating the file structure. The dataset corresponds to the root directory of a BIDS project. Within this root, data are organized hierarchically using subject (sub-) and session (ses-) directories. The official specification notes that if a dataset contains at least one subject with multiple sessions, the session directory structure SHOULD be applied consistently across all subjects in that dataset. This concept also underpins the requirement for a dataset_description.json file at the root, which provides high-level metadata about the entire collection.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Correctly identifying the boundaries of a dataset is crucial for running validation tools, as validators expect a specific root structure and metadata files. It ensures that data processing pipelines correctly traverse subject and session folders. Furthermore, distinguishing between a single dataset and multiple datasets (e.g., in multi-site studies) prevents structural errors and ensures that metadata accurately reflects the scope of the data being described.
example_scenarios: A single-site cognitive neuroscience study where 20 participants each undergo one scanning session. The dataset root contains 20 sub- folders, each with a func/ and anat/ directory.

A longitudinal intervention study where 15 participants are scanned at baseline and again at a 3-month follow-up. The dataset root contains 15 sub- folders, each with ses-baseline/ and ses-followup/ subdirectories.

A multi-center trial collecting data from three different hospitals. According to BIDS guidelines, each hospital's data may be organized as a separate dataset, or all data may be combined into a single dataset with a site entity or session structure.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: The definition of a dataset is consistent across BIDS versions (from v1.2.0 to v1.11.1). It is distinct from data type (e.g., func, anat, dwi) and modality (e.g., T1w, bold), which are functional groupings contained within the dataset. The dataset concept also relates to the participants.tsv and sessions.tsv files, which provide additional metadata at the subject and session levels respectively.

ai_enrichment.description: In the BIDS specification, DEPRECATED is a requirement level assigned to specific entities, suffixes, or metadata fields that are no longer recommended for use in new datasets. These items are retained in the standard solely to maintain backward compatibility and ensure that older datasets remain interpretable by modern tools.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: When BIDS Manager or the BIDS Validator flags a dataset element as deprecated, it indicates that the dataset uses an older convention. This generates a warning rather than an error, meaning the dataset is still valid and usable. The warning serves as a prompt to update the dataset to current standards, but it does not invalidate the data or prevent downstream processing.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Using deprecated entities or metadata can lead to validation warnings and may cause compatibility issues with future BIDS versions or updated parsing tools. Addressing deprecations ensures long-term interoperability, reduces ambiguity in data interpretation, and aligns the dataset with the most current best practices.
example_scenarios: A researcher uses a metadata field that has been marked as deprecated in the BIDS schema. The validator issues a warning suggesting a modern replacement, such as using the Sources field with BIDS URIs instead of the older field.

A dataset contains an entity or suffix that was part of an earlier BIDS draft but has since been removed or replaced. The validator recognizes it for backward compatibility but warns that it is deprecated.
A user follows an outdated BIDS tutorial or uses an older version of a DICOM-to-NIfTI converter that automatically populates deprecated metadata fields, triggering warnings during validation.
common_causes: Working with legacy datasets created under previous BIDS versions.
Using outdated conversion tools that generate deprecated metadata.
Following older documentation or tutorials that reference superseded entities or fields.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Review the specific warning message from the validator or BIDS Manager to identify the deprecated item and its recommended replacement. Update the filename or metadata JSON to use the current standard. If the dataset is historical and cannot be easily updated, the warning can typically be safely ignored or suppressed, as the data remains valid and interpretable.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: The BIDS schema explicitly defines a deprecated level for requirement levels, which validator tools map to a warning severity. This design choice balances the need for standardization with the practical reality of maintaining long-term access to historical research data. Deprecated items are never treated as errors in the validator, preserving the curator's intent while encouraging modernization.

retrieval_text:
In BIDS, Event refers to: Something that happens or may be perceived by a test subject as happening
at a particular instant during the recording.
Events are most commonly associated with on- or offset of stimulus presentations,
or with the distinct marker of on- or offset of a subject's response or motor action.
Other events may include unplanned incidents
(for example, sudden onset of noise and vibrations due to construction work,
laboratory device malfunction),
changes in task instructions (for example, switching the response hand),
or experiment control parameters (for example, changing the stimulus presentation rate over experimental blocks),
and noted data feature occurrences (for example, a recording electrode producing noise).
In BIDS, each event has an onset time and duration.
Note that not all tasks will have recorded events (for example, "resting state").
.
