title: ERROR INTERNAL_ERROR
summary: INTERNAL_ERROR: Internal error. SOME VALIDATION STEPS MAY NOT HAVE OCCURRED.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code INTERNAL_ERROR (error). Internal error. SOME VALIDATION STEPS MAY NOT HAVE OCCURRED. This is reported as an ERROR and makes the dataset invalid. INTERNAL_ERROR is a built-in validator issue rather than a schema rule check; it is raised by the validator itself while reading the dataset.

raw_content.message: Internal error. SOME VALIDATION STEPS MAY NOT HAVE OCCURRED.

ai_enrichment.description: The validator encountered an unexpected condition and stopped part of its work. Some validation steps did not run.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error in the validator rather than a statement about your dataset. The important consequence is that the report is incomplete: a clean result elsewhere does not mean the dataset passed those checks, only that they were not reached.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: An incomplete validation that looks complete is misleading. Treating the rest of the report as authoritative can send a dataset onward with real problems that were never examined.
common_causes: A file in a shape the validator did not anticipate.
A version mismatch between the validator and the schema it is using.
Resource limits, such as memory, on a very large dataset.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Update to a current validator version and run again. If it recurs, narrow the problem by validating subsets until one file reproduces it, then report that file to the validator's maintainers. Do not treat the rest of the report as a complete result.

title: ERROR NOT_INCLUDED
summary: NOT_INCLUDED: Files with such naming scheme are not part of BIDS specification. This error is most commonly caused by typos in filenames that make them not BIDS compatible. Please consult the specification and make sure your files are named correctly.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code NOT_INCLUDED (error). Files with such naming scheme are not part of BIDS specification. This error is most commonly caused by typos in filenames that make them not BIDS compatible. Please consult the specification and make sure your files are named correctly. This is reported as an ERROR and makes the dataset invalid. NOT_INCLUDED is a built-in validator issue rather than a schema rule check; it is raised by the validator itself while reading the dataset.

raw_content.message:
Files with such naming scheme are not part of BIDS specification. This error is
most commonly caused by typos in filenames that make them not BIDS compatible.
Please consult the specification and make sure your files are named correctly.

ai_enrichment.description: A file's name does not match any naming pattern the BIDS specification defines, so the standard has no rules to apply to it.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error. It does not mean the file is bad, only that BIDS does not recognise it. A file the standard cannot name is a file no BIDS tool can find.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: BIDS works because filenames are machine-readable. Tools locate data by constructing names from entities rather than by searching, so an unrecognised name is invisible to them regardless of what it contains.
common_causes: A typo or wrong case in an entity or suffix. Entity keys and suffixes are case-sensitive, so T1W is not T1w.
Entities in the wrong order. BIDS fixes the order of entities in a filename, and a correct set in the wrong sequence is still invalid.
An entity that is not permitted for that datatype and suffix, or a required entity left out.
Source data, notes, logs or derived files placed inside the raw dataset where the standard does not define them.
A file the standard genuinely does not cover, which belongs in sourcedata/, derivatives/ or an entry in .bidsignore.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Compare the name against the naming template for its datatype and suffix, checking spelling, case and entity order. If the file is a legitimate part of the dataset that BIDS does not define, move it to sourcedata/ or derivatives/ as appropriate, or list it in .bidsignore so the validator knows it is deliberate. Use .bidsignore for files that genuinely fall outside the standard, not to silence names that could be corrected.

title: ERROR NIFTI_HEADER_UNREADABLE
summary: NIFTI_HEADER_UNREADABLE: We were unable to parse header data from this NIfTI file. Please ensure it is not corrupted or mislabeled.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code NIFTI_HEADER_UNREADABLE (error). We were unable to parse header data from this NIfTI file. Please ensure it is not corrupted or mislabeled. This is reported as an ERROR and makes the dataset invalid. Applies to: match(extension, '^\.nii(\.gz)?$'). NIFTI_HEADER_UNREADABLE is a built-in validator issue rather than a schema rule check; it is raised by the validator itself while reading the dataset.

raw_content.message:
We were unable to parse header data from this NIfTI file.
Please ensure it is not corrupted or mislabeled.

ai_enrichment.description: The file is large enough to hold a NIfTI header, but the header could not be parsed.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error. The file is either not a NIfTI image, or it is one that has been corrupted or truncated in the header region.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Everything a tool needs to interpret the image, its dimensions, voxel sizes, orientation and data type, lives in the header. An unreadable header makes the voxel data meaningless even when the voxel data itself is intact.
common_causes: The file is corrupt or was truncated during copying.
The file is a different format that has been given a NIfTI extension.
A compressed file is damaged, so decompression yields garbage where the header should be.
A partially written file from an interrupted conversion.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Try opening the file with a NIfTI reader directly to confirm the diagnosis. Re-convert from the original source data if it is available, since a damaged header generally cannot be repaired. Check whether other files from the same conversion run share the problem, which points at the conversion rather than at this one file.

title: ERROR JSON_INVALID
summary: JSON_INVALID: Not a valid JSON file.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code JSON_INVALID (error). Not a valid JSON file. This is reported as an ERROR and makes the dataset invalid. Applies to: extension has  ".json". JSON_INVALID is a built-in validator issue rather than a schema rule check; it is raised by the validator itself while reading the dataset.

raw_content.message: Not a valid JSON file.

ai_enrichment.description: The file is not valid JSON and could not be parsed.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error. Because the file cannot be parsed, none of the metadata it contains is available to any check, so a JSON error usually suppresses many other findings that will appear once it is fixed.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Sidecars carry the metadata that makes a recording interpretable. An unparseable sidecar means the recording has no metadata at all as far as every downstream tool is concerned, even though the information is visibly present in the file.
example_scenarios: A sidecar ends with "EchoTime": 0.03, followed immediately by the closing brace. The trailing comma makes the whole file unparseable.
common_causes: A trailing comma after the last entry in an object or array. This is the single most common cause and is accepted by some editors.
A quote, brace or bracket that was never closed.
Single quotes instead of double quotes, or unquoted keys, which JSON does not permit.
Python or JavaScript literals written into JSON: None, True, False, NaN or Infinity rather than null, true and false.
Two sidecars concatenated, or a file edited by two processes at once.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Run the file through any JSON parser or linter; it will report the line and column of the first problem, which is the fastest way in. Fix the syntax and validate again, and expect new findings to appear afterwards that were previously hidden behind the parse failure.

title: ERROR GZ_NOT_GZIPPED
summary: GZ_NOT_GZIPPED: This file ends in the .gz extension but is not actually gzipped.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code GZ_NOT_GZIPPED (error). This file ends in the .gz extension but is not actually gzipped. This is reported as an ERROR and makes the dataset invalid. Applies to: match(extension, '\.gz$'). GZ_NOT_GZIPPED is a built-in validator issue rather than a schema rule check; it is raised by the validator itself while reading the dataset.

raw_content.message: This file ends in the .gz extension but is not actually gzipped.

ai_enrichment.description: The filename ends in .gz but the contents are not gzip-compressed data.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error. The extension is a promise about the format, and every tool that opens the file will try to decompress it and fail.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Software selects a reader from the extension. A plain NIfTI named .nii.gz will be handed to a gzip reader, which fails immediately, so the file is unusable despite containing perfectly good data.
common_causes: A file was decompressed and the .gz extension was left on the resulting name.
A file was renamed to add .gz without actually compressing it, usually to satisfy a naming convention.
A transfer step decompressed the file automatically in flight, which some web servers and sync tools do, while preserving the name.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Determine whether the contents are compressed. If they are not, either compress the file with gzip so the name becomes true, or remove the .gz from the name if the uncompressed extension is permitted for that file type. Do not rename to .gz without compressing.

title: ERROR NIFTI_TOO_SMALL
summary: NIFTI_TOO_SMALL: This file is too small to contain the minimal NIfTI header.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code NIFTI_TOO_SMALL (error). This file is too small to contain the minimal NIfTI header. This is reported as an ERROR and makes the dataset invalid. Applies to: match(extension, '^\.nii(\.gz)?$'). NIFTI_TOO_SMALL is a built-in validator issue rather than a schema rule check; it is raised by the validator itself while reading the dataset.

raw_content.message: This file is too small to contain the minimal NIfTI header.

ai_enrichment.description: The file is smaller than the minimum size a NIfTI header occupies, so it cannot be a valid NIfTI image whatever it contains.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error, and it is a size check rather than a content check: the file is too short to hold even the header, let alone image data.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: A NIfTI file this small holds no usable image. It is the signature of a conversion or transfer that failed and left a stub behind, which will otherwise be discovered only when an analysis tries to load it.
common_causes: The conversion producing the file failed or was interrupted.
The transfer or copy was truncated.
The file is a pointer, stub or placeholder from a data-sharing tool rather than the real content.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Re-create the file from its source data, or re-fetch it if the dataset uses a tool that stores content separately from the file tree. Compare the resulting file size against a comparable image from the same study to confirm it is plausible.

title: ERROR ORPHANED_SYMLINK
summary: ORPHANED_SYMLINK: This file appears to be an orphaned symlink. Make sure it correctly points to its referent.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code ORPHANED_SYMLINK (error). This file appears to be an orphaned symlink. Make sure it correctly points to its referent. This is reported as an ERROR and makes the dataset invalid. ORPHANED_SYMLINK is a built-in validator issue rather than a schema rule check; it is raised by the validator itself while reading the dataset.

raw_content.message:
This file appears to be an orphaned symlink.
Make sure it correctly points to its referent.

ai_enrichment.description: The file is a symbolic link whose target does not exist.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error. The dataset appears to contain the file, but opening it yields nothing.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: A broken link is worse than a missing file, because a file listing shows it as present. Datasets look complete, are shared, and then fail for whoever receives them.
common_causes: The dataset was copied without following links, so the links came across but their targets did not.
The link points outside the dataset to a location that exists only on the machine where it was created.
The target was moved, renamed or deleted after the link was made.
The dataset uses a content-addressed data-management tool and the file content has not been fetched.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Find where the link points and decide whether the target should be inside the dataset. For sharing, replace links with the real files, since links to locations outside the dataset never survive transfer. If the dataset is managed by a tool that stores content separately, fetch the content before validating.

title: ERROR FILE_READ
summary: FILE_READ: We were unable to read this file. Make sure it contains data (file size > 0 kB) and is not corrupted, incorrectly named, or incorrectly symlinked.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code FILE_READ (error). We were unable to read this file. Make sure it contains data (file size > 0 kB) and is not corrupted, incorrectly named, or incorrectly symlinked. This is reported as an ERROR and makes the dataset invalid. FILE_READ is a built-in validator issue rather than a schema rule check; it is raised by the validator itself while reading the dataset.

raw_content.message:
We were unable to read this file.
Make sure it contains data (file size > 0 kB) and is not corrupted,
incorrectly named, or incorrectly symlinked.

ai_enrichment.description: The validator could not read the file. It may be corrupt, truncated, locked by another process, or not the kind of file its extension claims.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error, and it is about the file itself rather than about BIDS. No rule could be evaluated, so a clean report for this file means nothing until the file can be read.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: An unreadable file will fail in exactly the same way for every analysis tool that comes after the validator. Finding it now, while the source data is probably still available, is far cheaper than finding it during analysis.
common_causes: The file is truncated because a copy or download did not finish.
The storage medium or transfer corrupted the file.
File permissions prevent reading, or another process holds the file open.
The extension does not match the actual format, so the reader for that extension fails.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Check the file size against the original, verify a checksum if you have one, and confirm you can open the file with the tool that normally reads that format. Re-copy it from the source if it is damaged. If the file reads correctly by hand, check its permissions.

title: ERROR BVEC_ROW_LENGTH
summary: BVEC_ROW_LENGTH: Each row in a .bvec file should contain the same number of values.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code BVEC_ROW_LENGTH (error). Each row in a .bvec file should contain the same number of values. This is reported as an ERROR and makes the dataset invalid. Applies to: extension has  ".bvec". BVEC_ROW_LENGTH is a built-in validator issue rather than a schema rule check; it is raised by the validator itself while reading the dataset.

raw_content.message: Each row in a .bvec file should contain the same number of values.

ai_enrichment.description: The rows of a .bvec file do not all contain the same number of values.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error. The three rows are the x, y and z components of the same set of directions, so they must be the same length.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Unequal rows mean the three components cannot be assembled into vectors. Readers either fail or silently pad, and padded directions point somewhere arbitrary.
common_causes: A value was lost or duplicated while the file was edited.
Inconsistent separators, such as a mixture of tabs and spaces, or two spaces between values.
A line wrapped when the file was copied through an editor or email.
Rows taken from different acquisitions.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Count the values in each row; the shortest or longest usually identifies where the problem is. Confirm that values are separated by single spaces and that no row has wrapped. All three rows must have exactly as many values as the image has volumes.

title: ERROR B_FILE
summary: B_FILE: .bval and .bvec files must be single space delimited and contain only numerical values.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code B_FILE (error). .bval and .bvec files must be single space delimited and contain only numerical values. This is reported as an ERROR and makes the dataset invalid. Applies to: intersects([extension], [".bval", ".bvec"]). B_FILE is a built-in validator issue rather than a schema rule check; it is raised by the validator itself while reading the dataset.

raw_content.message:
.bval and .bvec files must be single space delimited
and contain only numerical values.

ai_enrichment.description: A .bval or .bvec file is not formatted as BIDS requires. These files must be single-space delimited and contain only numbers.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error about the file's contents rather than its shape. Something in it is not a number, or the separators are not single spaces.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: These files are parsed by splitting on whitespace and converting to numbers. Anything else in the file stops the parse, and the diffusion directions become unavailable even though they are visible in the file.
common_causes: Tabs or multiple spaces used as separators instead of single spaces.
A header line naming the columns.
Comma separators, typically from a spreadsheet export.
Non-numeric placeholders such as n/a, NaN or empty entries where a number belongs.
Trailing whitespace or a stray character at the end of a line.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Open the file and confirm it contains only numbers separated by single spaces, with no header and no trailing characters. Note that these files are not TSV files despite sitting among them, so a spreadsheet is the wrong tool for editing them.

title: ERROR JSON_SCHEMA_VALIDATION_ERROR
summary: JSON_SCHEMA_VALIDATION_ERROR: Invalid JSON file. The file is not formatted according the schema.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code JSON_SCHEMA_VALIDATION_ERROR (error). Invalid JSON file. The file is not formatted according the schema. This is reported as an ERROR and makes the dataset invalid. Applies to: extension has  ".json". JSON_SCHEMA_VALIDATION_ERROR is a built-in validator issue rather than a schema rule check; it is raised by the validator itself while reading the dataset.

raw_content.message: Invalid JSON file. The file is not formatted according the schema.

ai_enrichment.description: The JSON file parses correctly but does not conform to the structure BIDS defines for it. A field has the wrong type, an unexpected shape, or a value outside what the standard permits.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error about content rather than syntax. The distinction matters: the file is readable, so the fix is to a specific field, not to the file's punctuation. The accompanying message names the field.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Type declarations are what let software consume metadata without guessing. A number written as a string, or a single value where a list is required, forces every reader either to fail or to apply its own coercion rules, and different tools coerce differently.
common_causes: A number written as a string, for example "2.0" rather than 2.0. This is common when metadata passes through a spreadsheet or a text template.
A single value where the standard requires an array, or an array where it requires a single value.
A value outside the set the standard allows for that field.
A misspelled field name, which can make a value appear under the wrong definition.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Read the message for the field name and the expected type, then look up that field's definition to see what it accepts. Correct the value's type or shape in the sidecar. Where the value came from an automated conversion, fix it at the source so sibling files do not carry the same defect.

title: ERROR NO_VALID_DATA_FOUND_FOR_SUBJECT
summary: NO_VALID_DATA_FOUND_FOR_SUBJECT: No BIDS compatible data found for at least one subject.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code NO_VALID_DATA_FOUND_FOR_SUBJECT (error). No BIDS compatible data found for at least one subject. This is reported as an ERROR and makes the dataset invalid. NO_VALID_DATA_FOUND_FOR_SUBJECT is a built-in validator issue rather than a schema rule check; it is raised by the validator itself while reading the dataset.

raw_content.message: No BIDS compatible data found for at least one subject.

ai_enrichment.description: A subject directory exists but contains no files the BIDS specification recognises.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error. The subject is declared by the presence of its directory, but nothing inside it is readable as BIDS data.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: A subject with no valid data will be counted by anything that enumerates subjects and then contribute nothing, which produces analyses with a participant count that does not match the data analysed.
common_causes: Every file in the subject has a naming problem, usually the same one, pointing at a conversion that went wrong for this subject.
The data sits one directory level too deep, or too shallow.
The directory holds only source data or notes, not converted data.
The directory is an empty leftover from a subject that was removed.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Look at what is actually inside the directory. If files are present but misnamed, correct the names, since fixing one usually fixes all of them. If the data sits at the wrong depth, move it so datatype directories are directly under the subject or session directory. If the subject has no data, remove the directory and the corresponding participants.tsv row.

title: ERROR WRONG_NEW_LINE
summary: WRONG_NEW_LINE: All TSV files must use Line Feed '\n' characters to denote new lines. This files uses Carriage Return '\r'.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code WRONG_NEW_LINE (error). All TSV files must use Line Feed '\n' characters to denote new lines. This files uses Carriage Return '\r'. This is reported as an ERROR and makes the dataset invalid. Applies to: extension has  ".tsv". WRONG_NEW_LINE is a built-in validator issue rather than a schema rule check; it is raised by the validator itself while reading the dataset.

raw_content.message:
All TSV files must use Line Feed '\n' characters to denote new lines.
This files uses Carriage Return '\r'.

ai_enrichment.description: A TSV file uses carriage return characters to end its lines. BIDS requires the line feed character.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error, and it is invisible in most editors, which display both line endings identically. The file looks completely normal while being non-conformant.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Parsers that split strictly on line feed treat a carriage return as part of the last field on each line. A column of values silently gains a trailing invisible character, so comparisons against it fail for reasons nobody can see.
common_causes: The file was written or edited on Windows, where the convention is carriage return plus line feed.
The file was exported from a spreadsheet application, which commonly uses the platform convention.
A version control system converted line endings on checkout.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Convert the file's line endings to line feed only. Most editors offer this as a setting, often shown in the status bar, and dedicated tools exist for it. If the file came from a spreadsheet, check the export options, and configure version control not to rewrite line endings for .tsv files.

title: ERROR MALFORMED_BVEC
summary: MALFORMED_BVEC: The contents of this .bvec file are undefined or severely malformed.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code MALFORMED_BVEC (error). The contents of this .bvec file are undefined or severely malformed. This is reported as an ERROR and makes the dataset invalid. Applies to: extension has  ".bvec". MALFORMED_BVEC is a built-in validator issue rather than a schema rule check; it is raised by the validator itself while reading the dataset.

raw_content.message: The contents of this .bvec file are undefined or severely malformed.

ai_enrichment.description: The contents of a .bvec file could not be interpreted at all.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error. The file cannot be read as gradient directions.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Gradient directions cannot be reconstructed from documentation, because they depend on the orientation convention used when the image was written. A lost .bvec usually means re-converting from source is the only reliable route.
common_causes: The file is empty or contains only whitespace.
The file holds text rather than numbers.
The file is binary, or a different file that was renamed.
The conversion wrote a partial file.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Look at the file's contents to confirm the diagnosis, then re-convert from the original source data. Avoid substituting a gradient table from documentation unless you can confirm which orientation convention it uses, since directions applied under the wrong convention produce plausible but incorrect tractography.

title: ERROR MALFORMED_BVAL
summary: MALFORMED_BVAL: The contents of this .bval file are undefined or severely malformed.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code MALFORMED_BVAL (error). The contents of this .bval file are undefined or severely malformed. This is reported as an ERROR and makes the dataset invalid. Applies to: extension has  ".bval". MALFORMED_BVAL is a built-in validator issue rather than a schema rule check; it is raised by the validator itself while reading the dataset.

raw_content.message: The contents of this .bval file are undefined or severely malformed.

ai_enrichment.description: The contents of a .bval file could not be interpreted at all.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error and a more severe form of a formatting problem: the file is not merely irregular, it cannot be read as b-values.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Without b-values, the diffusion weighting of each volume is unknown and no diffusion analysis can proceed.
common_causes: The file is empty or contains only whitespace.
The file holds text rather than numbers, for example an error message written by a failed conversion.
The file is binary, or is a different file that was renamed.
The conversion wrote a partial file.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Open the file and look at what is actually in it, which usually explains the failure immediately. Re-generate it from the original source data by converting again. If the source is unavailable, the b-values may be recoverable from the acquisition protocol, but the gradient directions in the .bvec generally are not.

title: ERROR SIDECAR_WITHOUT_DATAFILE
summary: SIDECAR_WITHOUT_DATAFILE: A json sidecar file was found without a corresponding data file.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code SIDECAR_WITHOUT_DATAFILE (error). A json sidecar file was found without a corresponding data file. This is reported as an ERROR and makes the dataset invalid. Applies to: extension has  ".json", suffix does not have  "coordsystem" || modality does not have  "emg". SIDECAR_WITHOUT_DATAFILE is a built-in validator issue rather than a schema rule check; it is raised by the validator itself while reading the dataset.

raw_content.message: A json sidecar file was found without a corresponding data file.

ai_enrichment.description: A JSON sidecar was found with no corresponding data file.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error. A sidecar describes a specific recording, and with the recording absent it describes nothing.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: An orphaned sidecar usually means a data file was lost, moved or renamed without its metadata following. That is worth knowing: the missing item is the recording, and the sidecar is the evidence it was once there.
common_causes: The data file was renamed and the sidecar was not, so the two no longer share a name.
The data file was deleted or was never copied across.
A typo in either name breaks the match, since a sidecar is paired to its data file by exact name.
A sidecar intended to be inherited by several files was placed at the level of a single recording rather than higher in the hierarchy.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Decide which of the two is wrong. If the recording exists under a different name, rename the sidecar to match it exactly. If the recording is genuinely gone, delete the sidecar. If the sidecar was meant to apply to several recordings, move it up to the subject, session or dataset level where the inheritance principle will apply it to all of them.

title: WARNING MISSING_SESSION
summary: MISSING_SESSION: Not all subjects contain the same sessions.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code MISSING_SESSION (warning). Not all subjects contain the same sessions. This is reported as a WARNING. The dataset remains valid, but the standard advises against the situation. MISSING_SESSION is a built-in validator issue rather than a schema rule check; it is raised by the validator itself while reading the dataset.

raw_content.message: Not all subjects contain the same sessions.

ai_enrichment.description: Not all subjects in the dataset contain the same sessions.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is a warning, and frequently it describes reality rather than a defect. Longitudinal studies routinely have participants who missed a session.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Uneven sessions across participants are worth noticing because they are equally consistent with a genuine dropout and with data that was never copied across. The validator cannot distinguish the two, so it reports the pattern and leaves the judgement to you.
common_causes: A participant genuinely did not attend a session, which is normal in longitudinal designs.
A session's data was not copied into the dataset, or was copied to the wrong participant.
Session labels are inconsistent between participants, for example ses-1 for one and ses-01 for another.
A session was excluded for quality reasons and its directory removed.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Compare the sessions present for each participant against your own records. Check the labelling first, since inconsistent labels make identical sessions look different. If a participant genuinely lacks a session, no change is needed and the warning is expected; document the absence in the README or in a sessions table so that a later reader knows it was intended.

title: ERROR INACCESSIBLE_REMOTE_FILE
summary: INACCESSIBLE_REMOTE_FILE: This file appears to be a symlink to a remote annexed file, but could not be accessed from any of the configured remotes.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code INACCESSIBLE_REMOTE_FILE (error). This file appears to be a symlink to a remote annexed file, but could not be accessed from any of the configured remotes. This is reported as an ERROR and makes the dataset invalid. INACCESSIBLE_REMOTE_FILE is a built-in validator issue rather than a schema rule check; it is raised by the validator itself while reading the dataset.

raw_content.message:
This file appears to be a symlink to a remote annexed file,
but could not be accessed from any of the configured remotes.

ai_enrichment.description: The file is a link to content held remotely by a data-management tool, and that content could not be retrieved.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error, but it often reflects the state of your local copy rather than a defect in the dataset. The dataset structure may be entirely correct while the file contents are simply not present yet.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Checks that read file contents cannot run without the contents. A validation report produced against unfetched files is silent about anything inside them, so it can look clean while saying almost nothing.
common_causes: The file content has not been fetched into the local copy yet.
The remote store is unreachable, or requires credentials that are not configured.
The content is no longer available at the remote location.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Fetch the content with whatever tool manages the dataset, then validate again. If fetching fails, check network access and credentials for the remote store. If you intend to validate structure only, be aware that content-dependent checks did not run.

title: ERROR EMPTY_FILE
summary: EMPTY_FILE: Empty files not allowed.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code EMPTY_FILE (error). Empty files not allowed. This is reported as an ERROR and makes the dataset invalid. EMPTY_FILE is a built-in validator issue rather than a schema rule check; it is raised by the validator itself while reading the dataset.

raw_content.message: Empty files not allowed.

ai_enrichment.description: The file exists but contains no data. BIDS does not allow empty files anywhere in a dataset.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error. An empty file is indistinguishable from a file that was never written, but it is worse than a missing file, because its presence asserts that data exists where none does.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: A zero-length file breaks every tool that opens it, and it hides the real problem: something upstream failed silently. It also makes a dataset look complete in a file listing when it is not, which is how an incomplete dataset ends up shared or archived.
example_scenarios: A conversion is cancelled mid-run, leaving a zero-byte NIfTI beside the completed ones.
common_causes: A conversion or export step failed part way and left the output file behind.
A copy or transfer was interrupted, or ran out of disk space.
A placeholder file was created by hand and never filled in.
A version-control or data-sharing tool fetched only file metadata, not content.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Find out whether the data exists elsewhere. If it does, copy it in again and confirm the file size is non-zero. If it does not, delete the empty file rather than leaving it: a dataset that is honestly missing a recording is valid, one that claims a recording it does not have is not.

title: ERROR BRAINVISION_LINKS_BROKEN
summary: BRAINVISION_LINKS_BROKEN: Internal file pointers in BrainVision file triplet (*.eeg, *.vhdr, and *.vmrk) are broken or some files do not exist.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code BRAINVISION_LINKS_BROKEN (error). Internal file pointers in BrainVision file triplet (*.eeg, *.vhdr, and *.vmrk) are broken or some files do not exist. This is reported as an ERROR and makes the dataset invalid. Applies to: intersects([extension], [".eeg", ".vhdr", ".vmrk"]). BRAINVISION_LINKS_BROKEN is a built-in validator issue rather than a schema rule check; it is raised by the validator itself while reading the dataset.

raw_content.message:
Internal file pointers in BrainVision file triplet (*.eeg, *.vhdr,
and *.vmrk) are broken or some files do not exist.

ai_enrichment.description: A BrainVision recording consists of three files, a header .vhdr, a marker .vmrk and the data .eeg. The internal pointers between them do not resolve to the files that are present.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error. The BrainVision header stores the names of its two companion files as text inside the header, so renaming any of the three breaks the set even though all three are sitting in the directory.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Readers follow the names written in the header, not the names on disk. A recording whose links are broken cannot be opened at all, which is a particularly easy mistake to make in BIDS because converting a dataset means renaming every file.
common_causes: The files were renamed to BIDS entities without updating the DataFile and MarkerFile entries inside the .vhdr, and the MarkerFile entry inside the .vmrk.
One of the three files was not copied.
The files were renamed by a tool that changed the names on disk without rewriting the header text.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Open the .vhdr in a text editor and check that its DataFile and MarkerFile entries name the .eeg and .vmrk files exactly as they exist on disk, then check the .vmrk names the .eeg the same way. Correct the text to match. Conversion tools built for BrainVision rewrite these pointers automatically, so converting again with a proper tool is usually safer than editing by hand.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: All three files must share the same BIDS name and differ only in extension. The .eeg and .vmrk are never opened directly; the .vhdr is the entry point.

title: ERROR HED_ERROR
summary: HED_ERROR: The validation on this HED string returned an error.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code HED_ERROR (error). The validation on this HED string returned an error. This is reported as an ERROR and makes the dataset invalid. Applies to: suffix has  "events", extension has  ".tsv". HED_ERROR is a built-in validator issue rather than a schema rule check; it is raised by the validator itself while reading the dataset.

raw_content.message: The validation on this HED string returned an error.

ai_enrichment.description: A HED annotation string failed HED validation. HED is a controlled vocabulary used to describe events; its strings are checked against the HED schema rather than against BIDS rules.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error, and it concerns the annotation rather than the BIDS structure around it. The events file may be perfectly well formed as a BIDS table while a HED string inside it is invalid.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: HED exists so that events can be searched and compared across datasets without knowing each study's private labels. An invalid string is not machine-readable, so the annotation gives up the benefit it was added for.
common_causes: A tag that does not exist in the HED schema version in use, often because of a spelling difference or a tag that was renamed between versions.
Unbalanced parentheses in a tag group.
A value given for a tag that does not take one, or omitted where one is required.
A tag used outside the part of the hierarchy where it is defined.
The annotation was written against a different HED schema version than the one the dataset declares.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Read the accompanying message, which names the offending tag and the reason. Check the tag against the HED schema version your dataset declares in HEDVersion, since a tag valid in one version may not exist in another. The HED validator and the online HED tools give more detail than the BIDS validator relays.

title: WARNING HED_WARNING
summary: HED_WARNING: The validation on this HED string returned a warning.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code HED_WARNING (warning). The validation on this HED string returned a warning. This is reported as a WARNING. The dataset remains valid, but the standard advises against the situation. Applies to: suffix has  "events", extension has  ".tsv". HED_WARNING is a built-in validator issue rather than a schema rule check; it is raised by the validator itself while reading the dataset.

raw_content.message: The validation on this HED string returned a warning.

ai_enrichment.description: A HED annotation string produced a warning during HED validation.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is a warning. The annotation is usable, but HED validation has found something worth reviewing, typically a stylistic or completeness issue rather than an outright error.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: HED warnings often point at annotations that are valid but less useful than intended, for example a tag that is deprecated or one that is more general than the situation allows. They affect how well the annotation supports later search and comparison.
common_causes: A deprecated tag that still validates but has a preferred replacement.
An annotation less specific than the schema allows.
Style issues in the annotation string.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Read the message for the specific concern and decide whether to act. These are worth addressing before sharing a dataset, since HED annotation is usually added precisely so that others can reuse the events.

title: ERROR HED_INTERNAL_ERROR
summary: HED_INTERNAL_ERROR: An internal error occurred during HED validation.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code HED_INTERNAL_ERROR (error). An internal error occurred during HED validation. This is reported as an ERROR and makes the dataset invalid. Applies to: suffix has  "events", extension has  ".tsv". HED_INTERNAL_ERROR is a built-in validator issue rather than a schema rule check; it is raised by the validator itself while reading the dataset.

raw_content.message: An internal error occurred during HED validation.

ai_enrichment.description: The HED validator encountered an internal error while checking an annotation.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error in the HED validation tooling rather than a statement about your annotation. The consequence is that the annotation was not fully checked.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: An annotation that was never checked may still be invalid. Treating the absence of a finding as a pass is unsafe here.
common_causes: A version mismatch between the HED validator and the declared schema version.
An annotation in a form the validator did not anticipate.
The declared HED schema could not be retrieved.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Update the validator and its HED components and run again. Confirm that the HEDVersion declared in dataset_description.json names a schema version that exists and can be fetched. If the error persists, validate the annotations with the standalone HED tools, which report more detail.

title: WARNING HED_INTERNAL_WARNING
summary: HED_INTERNAL_WARNING: An internal warning occurred during HED validation.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code HED_INTERNAL_WARNING (warning). An internal warning occurred during HED validation. This is reported as a WARNING. A UTF-16 file, which some Windows tools produce by default.

ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Re-save the file as UTF-8. Most editors expose the encoding in the save dialogue or a status bar. Afterwards, check that accented characters and other non-ASCII text still read correctly, since a wrong-encoding conversion can corrupt them silently.

If the same signal source is used as reference for all channels (often called a "monopolar" recording), specify the signal source (typically an electrode name). issue.message:
File is missing B0FieldSource metadata, so it may not be possible to
perform susceptibility distortion correction on it.
B0FieldIdentifier metadata permits the flexible selection of images
for estimating B0 inhomogeneity fields, and B0FieldSource permits EPI
images to indicate the identifier of the estimated field to use.
If associations are fully specified with `IntendedFor`, there is no need to change this.

title: Metadata field: DwellTime
summary: 'DwellTime' (Dwell Time) is a BIDS JSON sidecar field holding a number, in s.
retrieval_text: DwellTime (Dwell Time) is a BIDS JSON sidecar metadata field. Actual dwell time (in seconds) of the receiver per point in the readout direction, including any oversampling. For Siemens, this corresponds to DICOM field 0019, 1018 (in ns). This value is necessary for the optional readout distortion correction of anatomicals in the HCP Pipelines. It also usefully provides a handle on the readout bandwidth, which isn't captured in the other metadata tags. Not to be confused with "EffectiveEchoSpacing", and the frequent mislabeling of echo spacing (which is spacing in the phase encoding direction) as "dwell time" (which is spacing in the readout direction). Its value is a number, in s. The DwellTime field is RECOMMENDED when the file belongs to the mri modality and the file is a NIfTI image (.nii or .nii.gz). In a JSON sidecar it is written as "DwellTime": <value>.

title: Metadata field: EMGPlacementSchemeDescription
summary: 'EMGPlacementSchemeDescription' (EMG Placement Scheme Description) is a BIDS JSON sidecar field holding a string.
retrieval_text: EMGPlacementSchemeDescription (EMG Placement Scheme Description) is a BIDS JSON sidecar metadata field. Additional details of the approach to EMG sensor placement. Descriptions SHOULD NOT simply give the name of the targeted muscle (use the target_muscle column in *_channels.tsv for that), but rather SHOULD reflect the process used by the researcher(s) when placing electrodes. For example, EMG electrode sites may be chosen by *measured distance* from anatomical landmarks, by *visual reference* to (parts of) target muscles, by *palpation* of the skin to locate target muscles, or by *functional localization* (temporary electrode placement at several sites during prescribed behavior, until a site yielding strong EMG signal is found). Its value is a string. The EMGPlacementSchemeDescription field is REQUIRED when the file is in the emg datatype directory and the file's suffix is emg and sidecar.EMGPlacementScheme == "Other". The EMGPlacementSchemeDescription field is OPTIONAL when the file is in the emg datatype directory and the file's suffix is emg. In a JSON sidecar it is written as "EMGPlacementSchemeDescription": <value>.

If different channels have different reference electrodes, this field SHOULD contain the string "ChannelSpecific" and each channel's reference SHOULD be given in the reference column of *_channels.tsv. title: Metadata field: HardwareFilters
summary: 'HardwareFilters' (Hardware Filters) is a BIDS JSON sidecar field holding a object or a string.
retrieval_text: HardwareFilters (Hardware Filters) is a BIDS JSON sidecar metadata field. Object of temporal hardware filters applied, or "n/a" if the data is not available. Each key-value pair in the JSON object is a name of the filter and an object in which its parameters are defined as key-value pairs. For example, {"Highpass RC filter": {"Half amplitude cutoff (Hz)": 0.0159, "Roll-off": "6dB/Octave"}}. Its value is a object or a string. Allowed values: n/a. The HardwareFilters field is RECOMMENDED when the file is in the eeg datatype directory and the file's suffix is eeg; or when the file is in the emg datatype directory and the file's suffix is emg; or when the file is in the ieeg datatype directory and the file's suffix is ieeg; or when the file is in the meg datatype directory and "task" in entities and the file's suffix is meg, and 1 further context(s). In a JSON sidecar it is written as "HardwareFilters": <value>.

raw_content.name: HardwareFilters
raw_content.description:
Object of temporal hardware filters applied, or `"n/a"` if the data is not
available. Each key-value pair in the JSON object is a name of the filter and
an object in which its parameters are defined as key-value pairs.

0.0159, "Roll-off": "6dB/Octave"}}`.

title: Metadata field: HeadCoilCoordinates
summary: 'HeadCoilCoordinates' (Head Coil Coordinates) is a BIDS JSON sidecar field holding a object.
retrieval_text: HeadCoilCoordinates (Head Coil Coordinates) is a BIDS JSON sidecar metadata field. Key-value pairs describing head localization coil labels and their coordinates, interpreted following the HeadCoilCoordinateSystem (for example, {"NAS": [12.7,21.3,13.9], "LPA": [5.2,11.3,9.6], "RPA": [20.2,11.3,9.1]}). Note that coils are not always placed at locations that have a known anatomical name (for example, for Neuromag/Elekta/MEGIN, Yokogawa systems); in that case generic labels can be used (for example, {"coil1": [12.2,21.3,12.3], "coil2": [6.7,12.3,8.6], "coil3": [21.9,11.0,8.1]}). Each array MUST contain three numeric values corresponding to x, y, and z axis of the coordinate system in that exact order. Its value is a object. No sidecar rule group in this schema version makes HeadCoilCoordinates required or recommended, so it is optional wherever it is permitted. In a JSON sidecar it is written as "HeadCoilCoordinates": <value>.

Each array MUST contain three numeric values corresponding to x, y, and z

The TablePosition field is RECOMMENDED when the file belongs to the mri modality and entities.chunk and match(extension, '\.nii(\.gz)?$'). The TablePosition field is OPTIONAL when the file belongs to the mri modality and the file is a NIfTI image (.nii or .nii.gz). In a JSON sidecar it is written as "TablePosition": <value>.

The TaskName field is RECOMMENDED when the file is in the anat datatype directory and entities.task != null and the file is a NIfTI image (.nii or .nii.gz); or when the file is in the beh datatype directory and [suffix] shares a value with ["beh", "events"]; or when "task" in entities and ![suffix] shares a value with ["events", "channels", "markers"]; or when the file is in the pet datatype directory and "task" in entities. In a JSON sidecar it is written as "TaskName": <value>.

The TotalReadoutTime field is OPTIONAL when the file is in the fmap datatype directory and the file's suffix is epi and match(extension, '\.nii(\.gz)?$'). In a JSON sidecar it is written as "TotalReadoutTime": <value>.

raw_content.name: TotalReadoutTime

title: ERROR ACCEL_CHANNEL_COUNT
summary: ACCEL_CHANNEL_COUNT: ACCELChannelCount metadata must equal the number of channels with type ACCEL, as listed in channels.tsv.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code ACCEL_CHANNEL_COUNT (error). ACCELChannelCount metadata must equal the number of channels with type ACCEL, as listed in channels.tsv. When the file's suffix is nirs and the number of associations.channels.type, "ACCEL" > 0, it requires that sidecar.ACCELChannelCount == the number of associations.channels.type, "ACCEL". Failing this check is reported as an ERROR, which makes the dataset invalid. The check is named ACCELChannelCountReq in the BIDS schema. It concerns nirs data.

requirements.message: ACCELChannelCount metadata must equal the number of channels with type ACCEL, as listed in channels.tsv.

issue.message:
ACCELChannelCount metadata must equal the number of channels with type ACCEL,
as listed in channels.tsv.

ai_enrichment.description: The ACCELChannelCount field in the JSON sidecar does not equal the number of rows in the associated channels.tsv whose type column is ACCEL. The sidecar and the channel table disagree about how many ACCEL channels the recording contains.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error, so the dataset is not valid BIDS until the two agree. channels.tsv is the more reliable of the two, because it describes the recording channel by channel, while ACCELChannelCount is a summary that is easy to write once and never update. Treat the table as the truth and the count as the thing to correct, unless you have a specific reason to believe otherwise.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Analysis software uses these counts to decide how to interpret a recording: which channels to load, which to treat as data and which as auxiliary. A wrong count can mean channels are silently dropped from an analysis, or that non-brain channels are analysed as though they were data. It is also the first sign that the sidecar describes a different recording than the one it sits beside, for example after files were copied between sessions.
example_scenarios: A recording is preprocessed, two bad channels are removed and channels.tsv is rewritten from the cleaned data, but the sidecar still declares the original ACCELChannelCount.
common_causes: Channels were added to or removed from the recording, for example by dropping bad channels, and channels.tsv was regenerated while the sidecar ACCELChannelCount was left at its original value.

The type column in channels.tsv does not spell the channel type as BIDS requires. The type MUST be upper case and drawn from the list the standard defines, so a row typed as "accel" or with a vendor-specific name is not counted as ACCEL.
The sidecar was copied from another recording in the same study that had a different montage or a different number of auxiliary channels.
Auxiliary channels were counted into the wrong category, for example an eye channel recorded as EEG rather than EOG, so two counts are wrong at once.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Open the channels.tsv beside the recording and count the rows whose type column equals ACCEL. If that number is right, set ACCELChannelCount in the JSON sidecar to it. If the number is wrong, the table is what needs correcting: check that each channel's type is spelled in upper case and uses one of the channel types the standard defines, since a misspelled type is not counted. Do not adjust the count to silence the message without establishing which of the two is actually correct.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: Channel types in channels.tsv must be upper case and must come from the set the BIDS standard defines. A type that merely looks right, such as a vendor label or a lower-case spelling, is not recognised and is therefore not counted.

A placeholder value such as 99 used to mean unknown.

If it is real and the dataset will be shared, cap ages at 89 by recording 89 for every participant at or above that age, and say in the README or the participants.json that the column is capped. ai_enrichment.description: The number of values in the aslcontext.tsv volume list does not match the number of volumes in the NIfTI image. the aslcontext.tsv volume list holds one value per volume, so its length has to equal the number of volumes it describes.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error: the dataset is not valid BIDS until the lengths match. The check is comparing two independent statements about how many volumes the file contains and finding they disagree. One of them is wrong, and the validator cannot tell which.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: When the array length is wrong, there is no correct way to pair its values with the volumes. Software either fails outright or, worse, pairs them by position and silently attributes the wrong parameter to every volume after the first discrepancy. Results computed that way look plausible and are wrong.

common_causes: Volumes were removed from the image after the sidecar was written, for example dummy scans dropped during preprocessing, without the corresponding entries being removed from the array.
The acquisition was stopped early or restarted, so fewer volumes were saved than the protocol planned, while the sidecar still describes the planned acquisition.
The sidecar was copied from a similar run with a different number of volumes.
A single value was written where one value per volume is required, or one value per volume was written where a single value was expected.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Count the volumes in the image itself, then count the values in the aslcontext.tsv volume list, and establish which of the two reflects what was actually acquired. The mismatch is only between the per-volume form and a volume count, so switching to the single-value form is a valid fix when the parameter really was constant across the acquisition.

ai_enrichment.description: An AssociatedEmptyRoom field names a file that does not exist in the dataset. The field links a MEG recording to the empty-room recording used to characterise environmental noise.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error. As with other cross-file references, the link is a path written as text and breaks silently when files move.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Empty-room recordings are used to estimate the noise covariance for source reconstruction. If the link does not resolve, the noise model has to be estimated some other way or omitted, which changes source estimates without any obvious sign in the output.
common_causes: The empty-room recording was not included in the dataset.
The path is written at the wrong level. AssociatedEmptyRoom takes a dataset-relative path or a BIDS URI beginning bids::, not a subject-relative path.
Files were renamed after the sidecar was written.
The empty-room recording is stored under a convention the dataset does not follow, for example as a separate subject whose label differs from the one referenced.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Confirm the empty-room recording is present in the dataset, then check the form of the path: it is relative to the dataset root, or a BIDS URI. If the recording was never included, add it. Empty-room recordings are commonly stored as their own subject or session, so the path usually begins with a different subject directory than the recording that references it.

ai_enrichment.description: The dataset has a CITATION.cff file and dataset_description.json also has an Authors field. Only one of the two may state authorship.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error. It is not that either is wrong on its own, but that two authoritative author lists in one dataset can disagree.

ai_enrichment.description: A file with the beh suffix contains onset and duration columns, which are the defining columns of an events file.

ai_enrichment.description: A file with the bold suffix is not four-dimensional. A BOLD run is a time series, so it must have three spatial dimensions plus time.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error. A three-dimensional file named as bold is either a single volume that should not carry that suffix, or a time series that lost its time dimension somewhere in conversion.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Every functional analysis assumes it can index the fourth dimension. A three-dimensional bold file fails immediately in some tools and is misread as a single timepoint by others, which produces an analysis with no temporal information and no complaint.
common_causes: The conversion split a run into one file per volume instead of stacking them, which happens when the source series is not recognised as a time series.
The file really is a single volume, such as a single-band reference image, and has been given the bold suffix instead of its own.
A run was aborted after one volume was acquired, so the data is genuinely three-dimensional.
A preprocessing step that averages across time, such as computing a mean image, wrote its output back into the raw dataset.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Check how many volumes the image has. If the run was split into single-volume files, re-run the conversion so the volumes are stacked into one file. If the file is a reference image rather than a time series, give it the suffix that describes what it is, since a single-band reference has its own. If it is a derived image such as a temporal mean, move it into derivatives/ rather than leaving it among the raw data.

The dataset is still valid, but the standard recommends against it. The check is named BolusCutOffDelayTimeGreater in the BIDS schema. It concerns asl data.

requirements.message: 'BolusCutOffDelayTime' is greater than 10. Are you sure it's expressed in seconds?

issue.message: 'BolusCutOffDelayTime' is greater than 10. Are you sure it's expressed in seconds?

ai_enrichment.description: BolusCutOffDelayTime carries a value greater than 10 seconds. BIDS expresses this field in seconds, and a genuine BolusCutOffDelayTime above 10 seconds seconds is rare enough that the validator asks you to confirm it.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is a warning, not an error: the dataset is still valid BIDS and the validator cannot tell a real long value from a unit mistake. It is flagging that the number looks like milliseconds. For most acquisitions BolusCutOffDelayTime falls under a few seconds.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Timing metadata is read by analysis software as seconds without further checking. A value that is 1000 times too large silently distorts anything derived from it, including slice timing correction, temporal filtering, design matrices and modelling of the haemodynamic response. Nothing downstream will warn you a second time.
example_scenarios: A converter copies BolusCutOffDelayTime from DICOM unchanged, so a sidecar records the value in milliseconds where BIDS expects seconds.
common_causes: The value was copied straight from a DICOM header or scanner console in milliseconds. BIDS requires seconds, so the number is 1000 times too large.
A conversion script wrote BolusCutOffDelayTime without applying the unit conversion its source format needed.
The field was filled in by hand from a scanner protocol printout, which usually reports milliseconds.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Check the value against the acquisition protocol. If it was taken from a DICOM header in milliseconds, divide by 1000 and write the result back into the JSON sidecar. If the long value is genuinely correct for this acquisition, leave it as it is: the warning is a prompt to verify, not a defect to remove, and there is no way to suppress it other than correcting the value.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: BIDS states all timing metadata in seconds. Most sources of the same information, DICOM in particular, state it in milliseconds, so this class of mistake is common and worth checking across every timing field in the sidecar rather than only the one reported.

ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error about file format. The b-value file is a single row of numbers separated by spaces.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Readers expect a specific shape and will either fail or misread a file with extra rows, potentially assigning b-values to the wrong volumes.
common_causes: The file was transposed, so one value appears per line. This is the most common form and is easy to spot by opening the file.

The .bvec content was written into the .bval file, which has three rows.

ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Gradient directions are three-dimensional vectors. A file with the wrong number of rows cannot be read as directions at all, and a transposed file can be misread as a much smaller number of volumes.
common_causes: The file is transposed, with one direction per line rather than one component per line. This is the usual cause.
The .bval content was written into the .bvec file, which has one row.
Extra blank or header lines.
Two files concatenated.

title: WARNING EMG_CHANNEL_COUNT_MISMATCH
summary: EMG_CHANNEL_COUNT_MISMATCH: The EMGChannelCount metadata does not match the number of channels with type EMG in the associated channels.tsv file.

When the file's suffix is eeg and type(sidecar.EMGChannelCount) != "null" and associations.channels.type, it requires that sidecar.EMGChannelCount == the number of associations.channels.type, "EMG". When the file's suffix is emg and type(sidecar.EMGChannelCount) != "null" and associations.channels.type, it requires that sidecar.EMGChannelCount == the number of associations.channels.type, "EMG". Failing this check is reported as a WARNING. The dataset is still valid, but the standard recommends against it. This code is reported from 2 separate checks in the BIDS schema (EMGChannelCountReq, EMGChannelCountReq), so it can be raised in more than one situation. It concerns eeg, emg data.

requirements.message: The EMGChannelCount metadata does not match the number of channels with type EMG in the associated channels.tsv file.

issue.message:

with type EMG in the associated channels.tsv file.

ai_enrichment.description: The EMGChannelCount field in the JSON sidecar does not equal the number of rows in the associated channels.tsv whose type column is EMG. The sidecar and the channel table disagree about how many EMG channels the recording contains.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is a warning: the dataset is still valid BIDS, but one of the two statements about the recording is wrong and downstream software may read either of them. channels.tsv is the more reliable of the two, because it describes the recording channel by channel, while EMGChannelCount is a summary that is easy to write once and never update. Treat the table as the truth and the count as the thing to correct, unless you have a specific reason to believe otherwise.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Analysis software uses these counts to decide how to interpret a recording: which channels to load, which to treat as data and which as auxiliary. A wrong count can mean channels are silently dropped from an analysis, or that non-brain channels are analysed as though they were data. It is also the first sign that the sidecar describes a different recording than the one it sits beside, for example after files were copied between sessions.
example_scenarios: A recording is preprocessed, two bad channels are removed and channels.tsv is rewritten from the cleaned data, but the sidecar still declares the original EMGChannelCount.
common_causes: Channels were added to or removed from the recording, for example by dropping bad channels, and channels.tsv was regenerated while the sidecar EMGChannelCount was left at its original value.

The type column in channels.tsv does not spell the channel type as BIDS requires. The type MUST be upper case and drawn from the list the standard defines, so a row typed as "emg" or with a vendor-specific name is not counted as EMG.
The sidecar was copied from another recording in the same study that had a different montage or a different number of auxiliary channels.
Auxiliary channels were counted into the wrong category, for example an eye channel recorded as EEG rather than EOG, so two counts are wrong at once.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Open the channels.tsv beside the recording and count the rows whose type column equals EMG. If that number is right, set EMGChannelCount in the JSON sidecar to it. If the number is wrong, the table is what needs correcting: check that each channel's type is spelled in upper case and uses one of the channel types the standard defines, since a misspelled type is not counted. Do not adjust the count to silence the message without establishing which of the two is actually correct.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: Channel types in channels.tsv must be upper case and must come from the set the BIDS standard defines. A type that merely looks right, such as a vendor label or a lower-case spelling, is not recognised and is therefore not counted.

title: ERROR EPI_WITH_BVALS_NEEDS_SMALL_BVALS
summary: EPI_WITH_BVALS_NEEDS_SMALL_BVALS: EPI field maps with b-values should include small (b<100) values.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code EPI_WITH_BVALS_NEEDS_SMALL_BVALS (error). EPI field maps with b-values should include small (b<100) values. When the file is in the fmap datatype directory and the file's suffix is epi and "bval" in associations, it requires that min(associations.bval.values) < 100. Failing this check is reported as an ERROR, which makes the dataset invalid. The check is named EPISmallBVals in the BIDS schema. It concerns fmap data.

requirements.message: EPI field maps with b-values should include small (b<100) values.

issue.message: EPI field maps with b-values should include small (b<100) values.

ai_enrichment.description: An EPI fieldmap has associated b-values, but none of them is small. A fieldmap acquisition used for distortion correction should include at least one low b-value volume, below 100.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error. The presence of b-values means the acquisition is diffusion-weighted, and distortion correction needs an essentially undiffusion-weighted volume to work from.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Registration between the fieldmap and the data being corrected relies on anatomical contrast. Strongly diffusion-weighted volumes have little of it and low signal-to-noise, so a fieldmap consisting only of high b-value volumes cannot be registered reliably.
common_causes: Only diffusion-weighted volumes were included when the fieldmap was assembled.
The b-zero volumes were separated into a different file.
The b-value file belongs to a different acquisition.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Include the low b-value volumes in the fieldmap acquisition, or use the acquisition that contains them. Check that the .bval file really corresponds to this file, since a mismatched b-value file is a common cause.

ai_enrichment.description: A scan with a task entity has no corresponding events.tsv file.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is a warning, and whether it matters depends entirely on the task. For a task with discrete trials it is a real omission. For a resting-state run, which has a task entity by convention but no events, it is expected and can be ignored.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: An events file is what makes a task run analysable: it says what happened and when. Without it, a task dataset records that something was done to the participant but not what. Timing information is also difficult to reconstruct later, since it lives in the stimulus software's logs rather than in the imaging data.
common_causes: The run is resting state, conventionally named with a task entity such as task-rest, and genuinely has no events. This is the most common case and needs no action.
Stimulus presentation logs were never converted into an events.tsv.
The events file exists but its entities do not match the recording exactly, so it is not paired.
The events file sits in the wrong directory.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Decide first whether the run has events at all. If it is resting state, ignore the warning. If it has a task, convert the stimulus software's log into an events.tsv with at minimum the onset and duration columns, onsets measured in seconds from the first stored data point. If a file already exists, check that its entities match the recording exactly, since an events file is paired with its recording by name.

summary: EVENT_ONSET_ORDER: The onset column in events.tsv files should be sorted.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code EVENT_ONSET_ORDER (warning). The onset column in events.tsv files should be sorted. When the file's suffix is events and the file extension is .tsv, it requires that allequal(sorted(columns.onset, "numeric"), columns.onset). Failing this check is reported as a WARNING. The dataset is still valid, but the standard recommends against it. The check is named SortedOnsets in the BIDS schema. It concerns events data.

requirements.message: The onset column in events.tsv files should be sorted.

issue.message: The onset column in events.tsv files should be sorted.

ai_enrichment.description: The onset column of an events.tsv is not sorted in increasing order.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is a warning. The standard recommends events be listed in the order they occurred, which makes the file readable and matches what most tools assume.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Some software reads events sequentially and assumes chronological order. More practically, an unsorted file is hard to inspect by eye, and out-of-order onsets often indicate that rows from different conditions or different runs were concatenated without being merged properly.
common_causes: The file was assembled by concatenating one block of rows per condition rather than merging by time.
The file was sorted by trial type, or by another column, before being saved.
Rows from two runs were combined.
A correction added rows at the end rather than in place.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Sort the rows by the onset column. Before doing so, check why they were out of order: if two runs were concatenated, sorting merges them into one timeline, which is not a fix. Onsets must be measured from the start of the recording the file belongs to.

ai_enrichment.description: An electrodes.tsv filename carries task, acquisition or run entities. Electrode positions rarely change between runs, so this level of specificity is usually unintended.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is a warning about file placement rather than content. The positions may be perfectly correct while being scoped more narrowly than they need to be.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: A file named with a run entity applies only to that run. If the electrodes did not move, the same positions then have to be duplicated for every run, and duplicated files drift apart when one is corrected and the others are not.
common_causes: The electrodes file was generated per recording by a conversion that copies the recording's entities.
The entities were copied from the data file without considering scope.
The electrodes genuinely were re-placed between runs, which is unusual.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Unless the electrodes genuinely moved, remove the task, acquisition and run entities from the electrodes filename so that one file covers every recording it applies to. Inheritance will then apply it to all of them. If positions really did change between runs, keeping the entities is correct and the warning can be left.

issue.message: 'fieldmap.nii[.gz]' file does not have an associated 'magnitude.nii[.gz]' file.

ai_enrichment.description: A fieldmap image has no associated magnitude image.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error. A fieldmap describes the field offset at each voxel but carries no anatomical contrast, so on its own it cannot be aligned to the images it is meant to correct.

ai_enrichment.description: The GYROChannelCount field in the JSON sidecar does not equal the number of rows in the associated channels.tsv whose type column is GYRO. The sidecar and the channel table disagree about how many GYRO channels the recording contains.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error, so the dataset is not valid BIDS until the two agree. channels.tsv is the more reliable of the two, because it describes the recording channel by channel, while GYROChannelCount is a summary that is easy to write once and never update. A wrong count can mean channels are silently dropped from an analysis, or that non-brain channels are analysed as though they were data. It is also the first sign that the sidecar describes a different recording than the one it sits beside, for example after files were copied between sessions.
example_scenarios: A recording is preprocessed, two bad channels are removed and channels.tsv is rewritten from the cleaned data, but the sidecar still declares the original GYROChannelCount.
common_causes: Channels were added to or removed from the recording, for example by dropping bad channels, and channels.tsv was regenerated while the sidecar GYROChannelCount was left at its original value.

The type column in channels.tsv does not spell the channel type as BIDS requires. The type MUST be upper case and drawn from the list the standard defines, so a row typed as "gyro" or with a vendor-specific name is not counted as GYRO.
The sidecar was copied from another recording in the same study that had a different montage or a different number of auxiliary channels.
Auxiliary channels were counted into the wrong category, for example an eye channel recorded as EEG rather than EOG, so two counts are wrong at once.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Open the channels.tsv beside the recording and count the rows whose type column equals GYRO. If that number is right, set GYROChannelCount in the JSON sidecar to it. If the number is wrong, the table is what needs correcting: check that each channel's type is spelled in upper case and uses one of the channel types the standard defines, since a misspelled type is not counted. Do not adjust the count to silence the message without establishing which of the two is actually correct.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: Channel types in channels.tsv must be upper case and must come from the set the BIDS standard defines. A type that merely looks right, such as a vendor label or a lower-case spelling, is not recognised and is therefore not counted.

ai_enrichment.description: The gzip header of a compressed file contains a non-empty comment field. Gzip stores a free-text comment alongside the compressed data.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is a warning with two distinct meanings, and it is worth working out which applies. It may be a disclosure risk, because the header can carry information from the machine where the file was compressed. It may also simply indicate that the file was not compressed reproducibly, so byte-identical inputs produce different files.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Gzip headers are not visible in any normal view of a dataset, so a free-text comment can travel with a shared file without anyone noticing. The same fields also prevent checksums from matching between two compressions of identical data, which breaks verification and deduplication.
common_causes: The file was compressed with a tool that records source metadata by default, which most command-line gzip implementations do.
The file was compressed as a separate step rather than written compressed by the conversion tool.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Recompress the file with the comment field suppressed. Most gzip implementations offer an option for this, and libraries that write compressed data directly usually leave these fields empty already. Before recompressing, check whether the existing comment field discloses anything sensitive, since that determines how urgent this is.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: This finding is about the compression container, not about the data inside it. Decompressing and recompressing changes nothing about the image or table the file holds.

issue.message: 'LabelingDuration' is greater than 10. Are you sure it's expressed in seconds?

ai_enrichment.description: LabelingDuration carries a value greater than 10 seconds. BIDS expresses this field in seconds, and a genuine LabelingDuration above 10 seconds seconds is rare enough that the validator asks you to confirm it.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is a warning, not an error: the dataset is still valid BIDS and the validator cannot tell a real long value from a unit mistake. It is flagging that the number looks like milliseconds. For most acquisitions LabelingDuration falls between roughly 0.5 and 2 seconds for arterial spin labelling.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Timing metadata is read by analysis software as seconds without further checking. A value that is 1000 times too large silently distorts anything derived from it, including slice timing correction, temporal filtering, design matrices and modelling of the haemodynamic response. Nothing downstream will warn you a second time.
example_scenarios: A converter copies LabelingDuration from DICOM unchanged, so a sidecar records the value in milliseconds where BIDS expects seconds.
common_causes: The value was copied straight from a DICOM header or scanner console in milliseconds. BIDS requires seconds, so the number is 1000 times too large.
A conversion script wrote LabelingDuration without applying the unit conversion its source format needed.
The field was filled in by hand from a scanner protocol printout, which usually reports milliseconds.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Check the value against the acquisition protocol. If it was taken from a DICOM header in milliseconds, divide by 1000 and write the result back into the JSON sidecar.
