Treat the table as the truth and the count as the thing to correct, unless you have a specific reason to believe otherwise.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Analysis software uses these counts to decide how to interpret a recording: which channels to load, which to treat as data and which as auxiliary. A wrong count can mean channels are silently dropped from an analysis, or that non-brain channels are analysed as though they were data. It is also the first sign that the sidecar describes a different recording than the one it sits beside, for example after files were copied between sessions.

The sidecar was copied from another recording in the same study that had a different montage or a different number of auxiliary channels.
Auxiliary channels were counted into the wrong category, for example an eye channel recorded as EEG rather than EOG, so two counts are wrong at once.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Open the channels.tsv beside the recording and count the rows whose type column equals MAGN. If that number is right, set MAGNChannelCount in the JSON sidecar to it. If the number is wrong, the table is what needs correcting: check that each channel's type is spelled in upper case and uses one of the channel types the standard defines, since a misspelled type is not counted. Do not adjust the count to silence the message without establishing which of the two is actually correct.

retrieval_text: Validation issue code MISSING_MAGNITUDE1_FILE (warning). 'phasediff.nii[.gz]' file does not have an associated 'magnitude1.nii[.gz]' file. When the file's suffix is phasediff and match(extension, '\.nii(\.gz)?$'), it requires that "magnitude1" in associations. Failing this check is reported as a WARNING. The dataset is still valid, but the standard recommends against it. The check is named FmapPhasediffWithoutMagnitude in the BIDS schema. It concerns fmap data.

requirements.message: 'phasediff.nii[.gz]' file does not have an associated 'magnitude1.nii[.gz]' file.

issue.message: 'phasediff.nii[.gz]' file does not have an associated 'magnitude1.nii[.gz]' file.

ai_enrichment.description: A phasediff image has no associated magnitude1 image.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is a warning rather than an error, but the practical consequence is similar: a phase difference map without its magnitude image is difficult to use for correction.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: The magnitude image provides the anatomical contrast used to register the fieldmap to the data being corrected, and is also what masking is typically derived from. Phase data alone is noisy outside the head and hard to align.
common_causes: The magnitude series was not converted alongside the phase series.
The magnitude image is present but named with different entities, so it does not pair.
Only the phase output of the conversion was copied into the dataset.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Convert the magnitude series from the source data and place it in the same fmap directory with the same entities as the phasediff file. Confirm that the phasediff sidecar's EchoTime1 and EchoTime2 correspond to the magnitude images.

title: ERROR MISSING_ONSET_COLUMN
summary: MISSING_ONSET_COLUMN: The physioevents.tsv.gz file declared a OnsetSource of {sidecar.OnsetSource}, but no such column was found in {associations.physio.path}.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code MISSING_ONSET_COLUMN (error). The physioevents.tsv.gz file declared a OnsetSource of {sidecar.OnsetSource}, but no such column was found in {associations.physio.path}. When the file's suffix is physioevents and the file extension is .tsv.gz and sidecar.OnsetSource, it requires that [sidecar.OnsetSource] shares a value with associations.physio.sidecar.Columns. Failing this check is reported as an ERROR, which makes the dataset invalid. The check is named OnsetSourceConsistency in the BIDS schema. It concerns eyetrack data.

requirements.message: The physioevents.tsv.gz file declared a OnsetSource of {sidecar.OnsetSource}, but no such column was found in {associations.physio.path}.

issue.message: The `physioevents.tsv.gz` file declared a `OnsetSource` of {sidecar.OnsetSource}, but no such column was found in {associations.physio.path}.

ai_enrichment.description: A physioevents.tsv.gz file declares an OnsetSource in its sidecar naming a column that does not exist in the file.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error. OnsetSource points at the column holding event onsets, and it points at nothing.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Without a resolvable onset column, the events in the file cannot be placed in time at all, so they cannot be related to the recording they accompany.
common_causes: The column name in OnsetSource is spelled differently from the column header.
The column was renamed in the file without the sidecar being updated.
The sidecar was copied from a recording whose columns differ.
Case differences between the declared name and the header.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Compare the OnsetSource value against the column headers in the file exactly, including case and any surrounding whitespace. Correct whichever is wrong so the declared name matches a real column.

title: ERROR MISSING_RESOLUTION_DESCRIPTION
summary: MISSING_RESOLUTION_DESCRIPTION: The Resolution metadata object does not contain an entry for the file's res-<label> entity.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code MISSING_RESOLUTION_DESCRIPTION (error). The Resolution metadata object does not contain an entry for the file's res-<label> entity. When dataset.dataset_description.DatasetType == "derivative" and [modality] shares a value with ["mri", "pet"] and match(extension, '^\.nii(\.gz)?$') and type(entities.resolution) != 'null' and type(sidecar.Resolution) == "object", it requires that entities.resolution in sidecar.Resolution. Failing this check is reported as an ERROR, which makes the dataset invalid. The check is named ResInSidecar in the BIDS schema. It concerns common_derivatives data.

requirements.message: The Resolution metadata object does not contain an entry for the file's res-<label> entity.

issue.message:
The Resolution metadata object does not contain an entry for the file's
res-<label> entity.

ai_enrichment.description: A derivative file carries a res entity, but the Resolution metadata object in its sidecar has no entry describing that res label.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error. The entity is a short label, and the metadata is where the label's meaning is defined. Without the entry, the label names nothing.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Labels such as res-1 or res-hi are arbitrary strings chosen by whoever made the derivative. Their meaning exists only in the Resolution object, so an undefined label leaves the file's resolution undocumented.
common_causes: The res entity was added to filenames without the corresponding metadata entry.
The label in the filename does not exactly match the key in the Resolution object.
The sidecar was copied from a derivative using different resolution labels.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Add an entry to the Resolution object in the sidecar keyed by exactly the res label used in the filename, with a description of what that resolution is. Check the spelling and case, since the key must match the label exactly.

title: ERROR MRS_MATRIX_SIZE
summary: MRS_MATRIX_SIZE: MatrixSize metadata must match NIfTI header field dim[1:4].
retrieval_text: Validation issue code MRS_MATRIX_SIZE (error). MatrixSize metadata must match NIfTI header field dim[1:4]. When the file is in the mrs datatype directory and type(nifti_header) != "null" and type(sidecar.MatrixSize) != "null", it requires that sidecar.MatrixSize[0] == nifti_header.dim[1] and sidecar.MatrixSize[1] == nifti_header.dim[2] and sidecar.MatrixSize[2] == nifti_header.dim[3]. Failing this check is reported as an ERROR, which makes the dataset invalid. The check is named MRSMatrixSize in the BIDS schema. It concerns mrs data.

requirements.message: MatrixSize metadata must match NIfTI header field dim[1:4].

expression: sidecar.MatrixSize[0] == nifti_header.dim[1] AND sidecar.MatrixSize[1] == nifti_header.dim[2] AND sidecar.MatrixSize[2] == nifti_header.dim[3]

issue.message: MatrixSize metadata must match NIfTI header field `dim[1:4]`.

ai_enrichment.description: The MatrixSize metadata of a magnetic resonance spectroscopy file does not match the first three dimensions of the NIfTI header.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error. The metadata and the image header state the same spatial extent and disagree.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: For spectroscopy, the spatial dimensions determine how voxels are laid out relative to anatomy. A mismatch means the metadata describes a different acquisition geometry than the file contains, so spectra cannot be placed reliably.
common_causes: The sidecar was copied from an acquisition with a different matrix.
The image was reshaped or resampled after the sidecar was written.
The dimensions were written in a different order than the header uses.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Read the first three dimensions from the NIfTI header and compare them against MatrixSize. Check the ordering before assuming the values are wrong, since a transposed but otherwise correct triple is a common cause. Correct whichever does not match the acquisition.

title: ERROR MRS_NIFTI_CONSISTENCY
summary: MRS_NIFTI_CONSISTENCY: ResonantNucleus and/or SpectrometerFrequency fields are inconsistent between the NIfTI-MRS header extension and the BIDS sidecar.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code MRS_NIFTI_CONSISTENCY (error). ResonantNucleus and/or SpectrometerFrequency fields are inconsistent between the NIfTI-MRS header extension and the BIDS sidecar. When the file is in the mrs datatype directory and type(nifti_header.mrs) != "null", it requires that sidecar.ResonantNucleus == nifti_header.mrs.ResonantNucleus and sidecar.SpectrometerFrequency == nifti_header.mrs.SpectrometerFrequency. Failing this check is reported as an ERROR, which makes the dataset invalid. The check is named MRSNiftiConsistency in the BIDS schema. It concerns mrs data.

requirements.message: ResonantNucleus and/or SpectrometerFrequency fields are inconsistent between the NIfTI-MRS header extension and the BIDS sidecar.

issue.message:
ResonantNucleus and/or SpectrometerFrequency fields are inconsistent
between the NIfTI-MRS header extension and the BIDS sidecar.

ai_enrichment.description: The ResonantNucleus or SpectrometerFrequency fields are inconsistent between the JSON sidecar and the NIfTI-MRS header extension.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error. Spectroscopy data carries these parameters in two places, and they disagree.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: The resonant nucleus and the spectrometer frequency together set the frequency axis of every spectrum. If they are inconsistent, chemical shifts are computed against the wrong reference, so peaks are assigned to the wrong metabolites.
common_causes: The sidecar was written by hand or from a template rather than from the data.
The sidecar was copied from an acquisition on a different scanner or with a different nucleus.
A conversion wrote the header extension and the sidecar from different sources.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Take the values from the NIfTI-MRS header extension, which is written directly from the acquisition, and make the sidecar agree with it unless you have specific reason to believe the extension is wrong. Confirm the nucleus matches the acquisition, since a proton acquisition described as another nucleus shifts the whole frequency axis.

title: ERROR MULTIPLE_README_FILES
summary: MULTIPLE_README_FILES: There are multiple '/README' files (with different extensions) in this BIDS dataset. Only one '/README' file should exist.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code MULTIPLE_README_FILES (error). There are multiple '/README' files (with different extensions) in this BIDS dataset. Only one '/README' file should exist. When match(path, '^/README.*'), it requires that exists(["README", "README.md", "README.rst", "README.txt"], "dataset") == 1. Failing this check is reported as an ERROR, which makes the dataset invalid. The check is named DuplicateReadmes in the BIDS schema. It concerns general data.

requirements.message: There are multiple '/README' files (with different extensions) in this BIDS dataset. Only one '/README' file should exist.

issue.message:
There are multiple '/README' files (with different extensions) in this BIDS
dataset. Only one '/README' file should exist.

ai_enrichment.description: More than one README file is present at the dataset root, differing only in extension.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error. The dataset must have exactly one README, so that there is no question which one describes it.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Two READMEs are two descriptions of the same dataset with no rule saying which is current. In practice one is usually an abandoned draft, and a reader has no way to tell which.
common_causes: A README was converted from one format to another and the original was left behind.
Two people added a README in different formats.
A template README was left in place alongside the real one.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Decide which file is current, merge anything worth keeping from the other into it, and delete the rest. Keep exactly one file named README, with at most one of the permitted extensions.

title: WARNING NIFTI_DIMENSION
summary: NIFTI_DIMENSION: NIfTI file's header field for dimension information is blank or too short.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code NIFTI_DIMENSION (warning). NIfTI file's header field for dimension information is blank or too short. When type(nifti_header) != "null", it requires that the length of nifti_header.shape > 0 and min(nifti_header.shape) > 0. Failing this check is reported as a WARNING. The dataset is still valid, but the standard recommends against it. The check is named NiftiDimension in the BIDS schema. It concerns nifti data.

requirements.message: NIfTI file's header field for dimension information is blank or too short.

issue.message: NIfTI file's header field for dimension information is blank or too short.

ai_enrichment.description: The dimension field of the NIfTI header is blank or shorter than the image requires, so the header does not fully describe the image's shape.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is a warning. The image data may be intact while the header fails to describe it, which means tools have to guess.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Voxel data in a NIfTI file is a flat block of numbers. Only the header says how to fold it into a volume. An underspecified dimension field means different readers may fold it differently.
common_causes: The file was written by a tool that did not populate the header fully.
The header was edited or copied from another image.
The image was produced by a conversion from a format that carries less geometry information.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Re-convert from the original source data if possible, since a conversion tool that reads the source geometry will write a complete header. If the image cannot be re-converted, set the dimension fields explicitly using a NIfTI toolkit, taking the values from the acquisition protocol rather than guessing.

title: WARNING NIFTI_PE_DIRECTION_CONSISTENCY
summary: NIFTI_PE_DIRECTION_CONSISTENCY: The PhaseEncodingDirection and affine orientation indicate that the entity value (one of AP, PA, RL, LR, SI, IS) may be inaccurate.
retrieval_text:
Validation issue code NIFTI_PE_DIRECTION_CONSISTENCY (warning). The PhaseEncodingDirection and affine orientation indicate that the entity value (one of AP, PA, RL, LR, SI, IS) may be inaccurate. When type(nifti_header.axis_codes) != "null" and [entities.direction] shares a value with ["AP", "PA", "RL", "LR", "SI", "IS"] and sidecar.PhaseEncodingDirection, it requires that entities.direction[2 - the length of sidecar.PhaseEncodingDirection]
== nifti_header.axis_codes[index(["i", "j", "k"], sidecar.PhaseEncodingDirection[0])]. Failing this check is reported as a WARNING. The dataset is still valid, but the standard recommends against it. The check is named NiftiPEDir in the BIDS schema. It concerns nifti data.

requirements.message: The PhaseEncodingDirection and affine orientation indicate that the entity value (one of AP, PA, RL, LR, SI, IS) may be inaccurate.

issue.message:
The PhaseEncodingDirection and affine orientation indicate
that the entity value (one of AP, PA, RL, LR, SI, IS) may be inaccurate.

ai_enrichment.description: The PhaseEncodingDirection in the sidecar and the image's own orientation imply a phase-encoding axis that does not match the value of the dir entity in the filename.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is a warning about a disagreement between the filename and the metadata. Two independent statements are being made about the same fact and they do not agree.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Susceptibility distortion correction reverses distortion along the phase-encoding axis and relies on knowing its direction. Getting the direction wrong does not fail: it applies the correction backwards, roughly doubling the distortion it was meant to remove.
common_causes: The dir entity was assigned by hand or by convention rather than derived from the acquisition, and does not match the data.
PhaseEncodingDirection was copied from another acquisition with the opposite polarity, which is easy in a pair of opposed-polarity scans.
The image orientation differs from what the converter assumed when it translated the scanner's axis convention.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Establish which acquisition each file really is by returning to the source data or the protocol, then make the filename and the sidecar agree with it. In an opposed-polarity pair, confirm the two files are not swapped, since that is the usual cause and it makes both files wrong at once.

title: WARNING NIFTI_PIXDIM
summary: NIFTI_PIXDIM: NIfTI file indicates 0-sized voxels.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code NIFTI_PIXDIM (warning). NIfTI file indicates 0-sized voxels. When suffix != 'pet' and type(nifti_header) != "null", it requires that min(nifti_header.voxel_sizes) > 0. Failing this check is reported as a WARNING. The dataset is still valid, but the standard recommends against it. The check is named NiftiPixdim in the BIDS schema. It concerns nifti data.

requirements.message: NIfTI file indicates 0-sized voxels.

issue.message: NIfTI file indicates 0-sized voxels.

ai_enrichment.description: The NIfTI header reports voxel sizes of zero. A voxel with no extent cannot describe a real image.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is a warning about the header rather than the voxel data. The image may display correctly while carrying no usable information about scale.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Voxel size is how anatomical distance is recovered from array indices. With zero voxel sizes, spatial smoothing, registration, volume measurement and any report in millimetres are all either impossible or wrong.
common_causes: The writing tool left the voxel size fields unset.
A header was constructed by hand or copied from an incompatible image.
A conversion from a source format that did not expose voxel dimensions.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Re-convert from the original data, which is the reliable fix because the source carries the true voxel geometry. Only if that is impossible, set the voxel dimensions from the acquisition protocol with a NIfTI toolkit, and record that the geometry was reconstructed rather than read.

title: WARNING NIFTI_PIXDIM_PET
summary: NIFTI_PIXDIM_PET: NIfTI file indicates 0-sized voxels along spatial axes.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code NIFTI_PIXDIM_PET (warning). NIfTI file indicates 0-sized voxels along spatial axes. When the file's suffix is pet and type(nifti_header) != "null", it requires that min([nifti_header.pixdim[1], nifti_header.pixdim[2], nifti_header.pixdim[3]]) > 0. Failing this check is reported as a WARNING. The dataset is still valid, but the standard recommends against it. The check is named NiftiPixdimPET in the BIDS schema. It concerns nifti data.

requirements.message: NIfTI file indicates 0-sized voxels along spatial axes.

issue.message: NIfTI file indicates 0-sized voxels along spatial axes.

ai_enrichment.description: A PET image reports voxel sizes of zero along its spatial axes.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is a warning with the same meaning as a zero voxel size in any other image, reported separately because PET images are checked only on their spatial axes.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Quantitative PET analysis depends on knowing the volume each voxel represents. Without voxel sizes, concentrations, regional statistics and any coregistration with an anatomical image are unreliable.
common_causes: The reconstruction or conversion did not carry voxel geometry into the NIfTI header.
The image was converted from a format whose geometry was not read correctly.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Re-convert from the original reconstruction output using a tool that reads its geometry. If the image must be repaired in place, take the voxel sizes from the reconstruction parameters, not from a similar scan.

title: WARNING NIFTI_UNIT
summary: NIFTI_UNIT: NIfTI file's header field for unit information for x, y, z, and t dimensions is underspecified.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code NIFTI_UNIT (warning). NIfTI file's header field for unit information for x, y, z, and t dimensions is underspecified. When type(nifti_header) != "null", it requires that nifti_header.xyzt_units.xyz != 'unknown' and nifti_header.dim[0] < 4 or nifti_header.xyzt_units.t != 'unknown'. Failing this check is reported as a WARNING. The dataset is still valid, but the standard recommends against it. The check is named NiftiUnit in the BIDS schema. It concerns nifti data.

requirements.message: NIfTI file's header field for unit information for x, y, z, and t dimensions is underspecified.

issue.message: NIfTI file's header field for unit information for x, y, z, and t dimensions is underspecified.

ai_enrichment.description: The NIfTI header does not fully specify the units for the spatial and temporal dimensions.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is a warning. Readers will apply a default, usually millimetres and seconds, which is normally right but is an assumption rather than a fact the file states.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: If an image was written in different units and the header does not say so, every spatial measurement taken from it is wrong by a constant factor, and nothing in the file reveals it.
common_causes: The writing tool left the units field unset.
A conversion that did not propagate unit information.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Set the units field with a NIfTI toolkit after confirming what the image actually uses, or re-convert from source. Before doing either, check that the voxel sizes are plausible when read as millimetres, since that is the assumption everything downstream is already making.

title: ERROR NIRS_CHANNEL_COUNT
summary: NIRS_CHANNEL_COUNT: NIRSChannelCount metadata must equal the number of channels with type NIRS*, as listed in channels.tsv.
retrieval_text:
Validation issue code NIRS_CHANNEL_COUNT (error). NIRSChannelCount metadata must equal the number of channels with type NIRS*, as listed in channels.tsv. When the file is in the nirs datatype directory and the file's suffix is nirs and match(extension, '\.nii(\.gz)?$') and type(sidecar.NIRSChannelCount) != 'null', it requires that sidecar.NIRSChannelCount

+  the number of associations.channels.type, "NIRSCWMUA". Failing this check is reported as an ERROR, which makes the dataset invalid. The check is named NIRSChannelCount in the BIDS schema. It concerns nirs data.

issue.message:
NIRSChannelCount metadata must equal the number of channels with type NIRS*,
as listed in channels.tsv.

checks:
sidecar.NIRSChannelCount
== count(associations.channels.type, "NIRSCWAMPLITUDE")
+  count(associations.channels.type, "NIRSCWFLUORESCENSEAMPLITUDE")
+  count(associations.channels.type, "NIRSCWOPTICALDENSITY")
+  count(associations.channels.type, "NIRSCWHBO")
+  count(associations.channels.type, "NIRSCWHBR")
+  count(associations.channels.type, "NIRSCWMUA")

ai_enrichment.description: The NIRSChannelCount field in the JSON sidecar does not equal the number of rows in the associated channels.tsv whose type column is NIRS. The sidecar and the channel table disagree about how many NIRS channels the recording contains.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error, so the dataset is not valid BIDS until the two agree. channels.tsv is the more reliable of the two, because it describes the recording channel by channel, while NIRSChannelCount is a summary that is easy to write once and never update. Treat the table as the truth and the count as the thing to correct, unless you have a specific reason to believe otherwise.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Analysis software uses these counts to decide how to interpret a recording: which channels to load, which to treat as data and which as auxiliary. A wrong count can mean channels are silently dropped from an analysis, or that non-brain channels are analysed as though they were data. It is also the first sign that the sidecar describes a different recording than the one it sits beside, for example after files were copied between sessions.
example_scenarios: A recording is preprocessed, two bad channels are removed and channels.tsv is rewritten from the cleaned data, but the sidecar still declares the original NIRSChannelCount.
common_causes: Channels were added to or removed from the recording, for example by dropping bad channels, and channels.tsv was regenerated while the sidecar NIRSChannelCount was left at its original value.

The type column in channels.tsv does not spell the channel type as BIDS requires. The type MUST be upper case and drawn from the list the standard defines, so a row typed as "nirs" or with a vendor-specific name is not counted as NIRS.
The sidecar was copied from another recording in the same study that had a different montage or a different number of auxiliary channels.
Auxiliary channels were counted into the wrong category, for example an eye channel recorded as EEG rather than EOG, so two counts are wrong at once.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Open the channels.tsv beside the recording and count the rows whose type column equals NIRS. If that number is right, set NIRSChannelCount in the JSON sidecar to it. If the number is wrong, the table is what needs correcting: check that each channel's type is spelled in upper case and uses one of the channel types the standard defines, since a misspelled type is not counted. Do not adjust the count to silence the message without establishing which of the two is actually correct.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: NIRS channel types begin with NIRS, for example NIRSCWAMPLITUDE. The count covers every channel whose type starts with that prefix, not only an exact match on the word NIRS.

title: WARNING NIRS_RECOMMENDED_CHANNELS
summary: NIRS_RECOMMENDED_CHANNELS: NIRS files SHOULD have an associated channels.tsv file.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code NIRS_RECOMMENDED_CHANNELS (warning). NIRS files SHOULD have an associated channels.tsv file. When the file's suffix is nirs and the file extension is .snirf, it requires that associations.channels != null. Failing this check is reported as a WARNING. The dataset is still valid, but the standard recommends against it. The check is named RecommendedChannels in the BIDS schema. It concerns nirs data.

requirements.message: NIRS files SHOULD have an associated channels.tsv file.

issue.message: NIRS files SHOULD have an associated channels.tsv file.

ai_enrichment.description: A NIRS recording has no associated channels.tsv file.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is a warning: the standard recommends rather than requires the file here. In practice a NIRS recording is difficult to use without it.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: NIRS channels are source-detector pairs at specific wavelengths. Which pair and which wavelength a channel corresponds to is not recoverable from the data file alone, so without channels.tsv the channels cannot be related to positions on the head.
common_causes: The file was not exported alongside the recording.
Its entities do not match the recording, so the two are not paired.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Add a channels.tsv beside the recording listing every channel with its name, type, wavelength and the source and detector it connects, together with the sampling frequency if it varies per channel.

title: ERROR NIRS_SAMPLING_FREQUENCY
summary: NIRS_SAMPLING_FREQUENCY: Sampling frequency must be defined in the sidecar, or else as a sampling_frequency column of channels.tsv.
retrieval_text: Validation issue code NIRS_SAMPLING_FREQUENCY (error). Sampling frequency must be defined in the sidecar, or else as a sampling_frequency column of channels.tsv. When the file's suffix is nirs and sidecar.SamplingFrequency == "n/a", it requires that associations.channels.sampling_frequency != null. Failing this check is reported as an ERROR, which makes the dataset invalid. The check is named NASamplingFreq in the BIDS schema. It concerns nirs data.

requirements.message: Sampling frequency must be defined in the sidecar, or else as a sampling_frequency column of channels.tsv.

issue.message:
Sampling frequency must be defined in the sidecar, or else as a sampling_frequency
column of channels.tsv.

ai_enrichment.description: The sampling frequency of a NIRS recording is not defined. It must be given either in the JSON sidecar or as a sampling_frequency column in channels.tsv.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error. NIRS allows the sampling frequency to be stated per channel, because channels can be sampled at different rates, but one of the two forms must be present.

ai_enrichment.description: The subject directories present in the dataset do not match the values in the participant_id column of participants.tsv.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error. participants.tsv is the dataset's own list of who is in it, and it disagrees with what is actually on disk. The mismatch can run either way: a listed participant with no directory, or a directory with no row.

If the identifiers do not line up, that information is attached to the wrong person or to nobody, which can silently misassign group membership in an analysis. Zero-padding differs between the table and the directories, so sub-1 and sub-01 do not match.
Only part of the dataset was copied, so directories are missing for participants that are legitimately listed.
Trailing whitespace in the column, which is invisible in a spreadsheet but makes the strings unequal.

ai_enrichment.description: The number of values in EchoTime does not match the number of volumes in the PDT2 image. EchoTime holds one value per volume, so its length has to equal the number of volumes it describes.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is a warning: the dataset remains valid BIDS, but the mismatch usually indicates a real bookkeeping mistake. The check is comparing two independent statements about how many volumes the file contains and finding they disagree. One of them is wrong, and the validator cannot tell which.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: When the array length is wrong, there is no correct way to pair its values with the volumes. Software either fails outright or, worse, pairs them by position and silently attributes the wrong parameter to every volume after the first discrepancy. Results computed that way look plausible and are wrong.
example_scenarios: Four dummy volumes are discarded from a run, so the image now has four fewer volumes than EchoTime has values.
common_causes: Volumes were removed from the image after the sidecar was written, for example dummy scans dropped during preprocessing, without the corresponding entries being removed from the array.
The acquisition was stopped early or restarted, so fewer volumes were saved than the protocol planned, while the sidecar still describes the planned acquisition.
The sidecar was copied from a similar run with a different number of volumes.
A single value was written where one value per volume is required, or one value per volume was written where a single value was expected.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Count the volumes in the image itself, then count the values in EchoTime, and establish which of the two reflects what was actually acquired. Correct whichever is wrong rather than padding or trimming the array to make the numbers agree, because padding produces values that are the right length and describe nothing real. A PDT2 file holds a proton-density volume and a T2-weighted volume, so EchoTime should carry one value for each.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: When a field may hold either one value for the whole file or one value per volume, both forms are legitimate. The mismatch is only between the per-volume form and a volume count, so switching to the single-value form is a valid fix when the parameter really was constant across the acquisition.

ai_enrichment.description: The PixelSize metadata of a microscopy image is inconsistent with the PhysicalSizeX, PhysicalSizeY and PhysicalSizeZ values in the image's own OME metadata.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error. The physical size of a pixel is stated in two places and the two disagree.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Everything quantitative in microscopy depends on pixel size: cell counts per unit area, distances, areas, volumes. An inconsistency means any measurement in physical units could be wrong, and there is no way to tell which of the two sources was used.
common_causes: PixelSize was entered by hand and does not match what the acquisition recorded.
The two are expressed in different units, so the same size reads as two different numbers.
The image was resampled or downscaled without PixelSize being updated.
The sidecar was copied from an image acquired at a different magnification.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Read the physical sizes from the image's OME metadata and compare them against PixelSize, checking units before values since a unit difference accounts for many of these. Set PixelSize to match, along with PixelSizeUnits. If the image was downscaled, the pixel size has changed by the same factor and must be recomputed rather than copied.

ai_enrichment.description: PostLabelingDelay carries a value greater than 10 seconds. BIDS expresses this field in seconds, and a genuine PostLabelingDelay above 10 seconds seconds is rare enough that the validator asks you to confirm it.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is a warning, not an error: the dataset is still valid BIDS and the validator cannot tell a real long value from a unit mistake. It is flagging that the number looks like milliseconds. For most acquisitions PostLabelingDelay falls between roughly 0.5 and 3 seconds for arterial spin labelling.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Timing metadata is read by analysis software as seconds without further checking. A value that is 1000 times too large silently distorts anything derived from it, including slice timing correction, temporal filtering, design matrices and modelling of the haemodynamic response. Nothing downstream will warn you a second time.
example_scenarios: A converter copies PostLabelingDelay from DICOM unchanged, so a sidecar records the value in milliseconds where BIDS expects seconds.
common_causes: The value was copied straight from a DICOM header or scanner console in milliseconds. BIDS requires seconds, so the number is 1000 times too large.
A conversion script wrote PostLabelingDelay without applying the unit conversion its source format needed.
The field was filled in by hand from a scanner protocol printout, which usually reports milliseconds.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Check the value against the acquisition protocol. If it was taken from a DICOM header in milliseconds, divide by 1000 and write the result back into the JSON sidecar. If the long value is genuinely correct for this acquisition, leave it as it is: the warning is a prompt to verify, not a defect to remove, and there is no way to suppress it other than correcting the value.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: BIDS states all timing metadata in seconds. Most sources of the same information, DICOM in particular, state it in milliseconds, so this class of mistake is common and worth checking across every timing field in the sidecar rather than only the one reported.

ai_enrichment.description: The number of values in PostLabelingDelay does not match the number of volumes listed in the associated aslcontext.tsv. PostLabelingDelay holds one value per volume, so its length has to equal the number of volumes it describes.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error: the dataset is not valid BIDS until the lengths match. The check is comparing two independent statements about how many volumes the file contains and finding they disagree. One of them is wrong, and the validator cannot tell which.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: When the array length is wrong, there is no correct way to pair its values with the volumes. Software either fails outright or, worse, pairs them by position and silently attributes the wrong parameter to every volume after the first discrepancy. Results computed that way look plausible and are wrong.
example_scenarios: Four dummy volumes are discarded from a run, so the image now has four fewer volumes than PostLabelingDelay has values.
common_causes: Volumes were removed from the image after the sidecar was written, for example dummy scans dropped during preprocessing, without the corresponding entries being removed from the array.
The acquisition was stopped early or restarted, so fewer volumes were saved than the protocol planned, while the sidecar still describes the planned acquisition.
The sidecar was copied from a similar run with a different number of volumes.
A single value was written where one value per volume is required, or one value per volume was written where a single value was expected.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Count the volumes in the image itself, then count the values in PostLabelingDelay, and establish which of the two reflects what was actually acquired. Correct whichever is wrong rather than padding or trimming the array to make the numbers agree, because padding produces values that are the right length and describe nothing real.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: When a field may hold either one value for the whole file or one value per volume, both forms are legitimate. The mismatch is only between the per-volume form and a volume count, so switching to the single-value form is a valid fix when the parameter really was constant across the acquisition.

ai_enrichment.description: The dataset has no README file at its root.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is a warning. The dataset is valid without one, but the standard recommends a README and most repositories require one before accepting a dataset.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: A README is the only place that explains the study in prose: what was acquired, why, what the task was, what the participants did, what is unusual about the data. None of that is expressible in metadata fields, and without it a dataset is very hard to reuse even when it is perfectly structured.
common_causes: The file was never written.
It is named differently, for example readme.txt in lower case or notes.md.
It sits inside a subdirectory rather than at the dataset root.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Add a file named README at the dataset root. It may carry no extension or one of .md, .rst or .txt. Describe the study, the participants, the tasks and anything a person reusing the data would otherwise have to guess. Length is less important than covering what the structured metadata cannot say.

ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error. The sidecar summary and the channel table disagree about how many short-separation channels the recording has.

ai_enrichment.description: The number of values in SliceTiming does not match the number of slices in the corresponding NIfTI volume. SliceTiming holds one value per volume, so its length has to equal the number of volumes it describes.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is a warning: the dataset remains valid BIDS, but the mismatch usually indicates a real bookkeeping mistake. The check is comparing two independent statements about how many volumes the file contains and finding they disagree. One of them is wrong, and the validator cannot tell which.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: When the array length is wrong, there is no correct way to pair its values with the volumes. Software either fails outright or, worse, pairs them by position and silently attributes the wrong parameter to every volume after the first discrepancy. Results computed that way look plausible and are wrong.
example_scenarios: Four dummy volumes are discarded from a run, so the image now has four fewer volumes than SliceTiming has values.
common_causes: Volumes were removed from the image after the sidecar was written, for example dummy scans dropped during preprocessing, without the corresponding entries being removed from the array.
The acquisition was stopped early or restarted, so fewer volumes were saved than the protocol planned, while the sidecar still describes the planned acquisition.
The sidecar was copied from a similar run with a different number of volumes.
A single value was written where one value per volume is required, or one value per volume was written where a single value was expected.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Count the volumes in the image itself, then count the values in SliceTiming, and establish which of the two reflects what was actually acquired. Correct whichever is wrong rather than padding or trimming the array to make the numbers agree, because padding produces values that are the right length and describe nothing real. SliceTiming holds the acquisition time of every slice within a volume, so it needs exactly one value per slice along the slice axis, not per volume.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: When a field may hold either one value for the whole file or one value per volume, both forms are legitimate. The mismatch is only between the per-volume form and a volume count, so switching to the single-value form is a valid fix when the parameter really was constant across the acquisition.

When the file's suffix is bold and the file is a NIfTI image (.nii or .nii.gz) and type(sidecar.SliceTiming) != "null" and type(sidecar.RepetitionTime) != "null", it requires that max(sidecar.SliceTiming) <= sidecar.RepetitionTime. Failing this check is reported as an ERROR, which makes the dataset invalid. The check is named SliceTimingGreaterThanRepetitionTime in the BIDS schema. It concerns func data.

ai_enrichment.description: SliceTiming contains one or more values larger than RepetitionTime. Slice times are measured from the start of the volume they belong to, so every value must fall within one repetition time.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error. A slice acquired later than the whole volume took is not possible, so either the slice times or the repetition time is wrong.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Slice timing correction shifts each slice's time series to a common reference using these values. Values outside the volume's own duration make the correction shift data by more than a whole volume, which misaligns the time series rather than aligning it.
common_causes: SliceTiming is in milliseconds while RepetitionTime is in seconds. This is the most common cause and it makes nearly every value exceed the repetition time at once.
SliceTiming was copied from an acquisition with a longer repetition time.
Slice times were measured from the start of the run rather than the start of each volume, so they grow throughout the acquisition.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Compare the largest SliceTiming value with RepetitionTime. If it is close to 1000 times too large, the array is in milliseconds and needs dividing by 1000. If the values increase steadily beyond the first volume, they are measured from the start of the run and must be re-expressed relative to each volume. Otherwise check whether RepetitionTime itself is wrong.

ai_enrichment.description: A Sources field names one or more files that do not exist in the dataset. Sources records the inputs a file was derived from.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error. The provenance chain the field records is broken at this link.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Sources is how a derived file states what it came from, which is the basis of reproducibility in derivative datasets. A reference that does not resolve means the chain cannot be followed back to the raw data.
common_causes: The source file is in a different dataset, for example the raw dataset that a derivative was computed from, and is referenced without a URI that can reach it.
Files were renamed in the source dataset after the derivative was computed.
The path is written at the wrong level. Sources takes dataset-relative paths or BIDS URIs.
The derivative was copied away from the dataset it was computed within.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Check the path form first: dataset-relative, or a BIDS URI beginning bids::. When the source lives in another dataset, use a BIDS URI with the named dataset form and declare that dataset in the DatasetLinks field of dataset_description.json, which is what makes a cross-dataset reference resolvable.

requirements.message: A stimulus file was declared but not found in the dataset.

issue.message: A stimulus file was declared but not found in the dataset.

ai_enrichment.description: An events file refers to a stimulus file in its stim_file column, but that file is not present in the dataset.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error. The reference names a file that does not exist.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Stimulus files are what make an experiment reproducible: without the actual images, sounds or videos presented, the events file records that something was shown but not what. Recovering them later is often impossible.
common_causes: The stimuli were not copied into the dataset. They belong in a /stimuli directory at the dataset root.
The paths in stim_file are written relative to the wrong location. They are relative to the /stimuli directory, so the column should not repeat stimuli/ in the path.
Filenames differ in case, which matters on most systems.
Stimuli were omitted deliberately for copyright reasons.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Create a /stimuli directory at the dataset root and place the stimulus files in it, then check that the stim_file values are paths relative to that directory. If the stimuli cannot be shared for licensing reasons, remove the stim_file column and describe the stimuli in the README, rather than leaving references that resolve to nothing.

ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is a warning, but in practice it usually means the validator is not looking at a BIDS dataset root at all.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Subject directories are how every BIDS tool enumerates participants. With none present, the dataset has no data any tool can find, whatever it contains.
common_causes: The validator was pointed at a parent directory, or at one level inside the dataset, rather than at the dataset root.
The subject directories are named without the sub- prefix, for example using bare identifiers or names.
Data is grouped by session or by datatype at the top level, with subjects nested inside, which is the reverse of the BIDS hierarchy.
The dataset holds only source data that has not been converted yet.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Confirm you are pointing at the directory that contains dataset_description.json. If you are, check the naming of the participant directories: each must be sub- followed by a label of letters and digits only, with no underscores, hyphens or spaces. If the hierarchy is grouped by session or datatype first, it has to be reorganised so that subject is the outermost level.

ai_enrichment.description: The onset of the last event in the events file falls after the end of the corresponding recording.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is a warning. Events are supposed to describe what happened during the recording, so an event after it ended is either mistimed or belongs to a different run.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: An event outside the recording cannot be modelled, and its presence suggests the events file and the recording do not correspond. The rest of the file's timings may be wrong in the same way.
common_causes: The events file belongs to a different, longer run.
The recording was truncated or stopped early while the events file describes the full protocol.
Onsets in the wrong unit or measured from the wrong reference point.
Events from several runs concatenated into one file.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Compare the last onset with the recording's duration, which is the number of volumes multiplied by the repetition time for imaging data. If the events file describes a longer session, check it belongs to this run. If the recording stopped early, keep only the events that fall within it and note the truncation in the README.

ai_enrichment.description: The onset of the last event falls in the first half of the recording, so the second half appears to contain no events.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is a warning about a pattern that is sometimes correct. A design with a long post-task period is legitimate; more often the events file is truncated.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: If the events file is incomplete, the unmodelled portion of the recording is treated as baseline, which biases the estimated response for every condition, not only the missing trials.
common_causes: The events file was truncated when it was written or exported.
The stimulus program crashed or was stopped part way while the recording continued.
Only one of several blocks was converted into the events file.
The events belong to a shorter run.
The design genuinely has a long period with no events.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Compare the last onset with the recording duration and against your protocol. If the design really does end early, no change is needed. If events are missing, recover them from the stimulus software's logs. If the session was interrupted, record that in the README, since the recording then contains a period that was never part of the experiment.

ai_enrichment.description: One or more event onsets fall more than 60 seconds before the start of the recording, indicated by large negative values.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is a warning. Negative onsets are permitted by the standard, for events that genuinely occurred before the first stored data point, but values this far back are unusual.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Onsets are measured from the first stored data point of the recording. Large negative values normally mean the events were timed against a different clock, so every onset in the file may be offset by the same amount, which shifts the whole design.
common_causes: Onsets measured from the start of the stimulus program rather than from the first stored data point, so the offset between the two clocks appears as a constant shift.
Dummy volumes were discarded from the recording without the onsets being re-referenced to the new start.
Timestamps in absolute wall-clock time rather than relative to the recording.
A genuine pre-scan training period, in which case the values are correct.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Look at whether all onsets share a similar offset, which points to a timing reference problem affecting the whole file rather than a few stray rows. Re-reference the onsets to the first stored data point of the recording. If events legitimately preceded the recording, the negative values are correct and the warning can be left.

ai_enrichment.description: One or more event onsets fall more than a month after the start of the recording.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is a warning. An onset that far out is almost certainly a timestamp rather than an elapsed time.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Onsets are elapsed seconds from the start of the recording. A value of that magnitude is an absolute time in disguise, usually seconds since an epoch, which means no event in the file is placed correctly.
common_causes: Onsets written as absolute timestamps, for example seconds since the Unix epoch, rather than as elapsed time.
Onsets in milliseconds or microseconds rather than seconds.
A stray or corrupted value in one row.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Check whether the values are timestamps by looking at their magnitude and at the differences between them: if the differences are plausible while the values are enormous, subtract the recording's start time from every onset. If the whole column is a fixed factor too large, correct the units. Onsets are always in seconds relative to the recording.

retrieval_text: Validation issue code T1W_FILE_WITH_TOO_MANY_DIMENSIONS (error). _T1w.nii[.gz] files must have exactly three dimensions. When the file's suffix is T1w and the NIfTI header could be read, it requires that the image has exactly 3 dimensions. Failing this check is reported as an ERROR, which makes the dataset invalid. The check is named T1wFileWithTooManyDimensions in the BIDS schema. It concerns anat data.

requirements.message: _T1w.nii[.gz] files must have exactly three dimensions.

issue.message: _T1w.nii[.gz] files must have exactly three dimensions.

ai_enrichment.description: A file with the T1w suffix has more than three dimensions. An anatomical T1-weighted image is a single volume.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error. The extra dimension means the file holds several images stacked together, which the T1w suffix does not describe.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Anatomical images are used as a reference space for everything else: registration targets, segmentation inputs, surface reconstruction. Tools expect one volume and will either fail or silently use only the first, so which image actually served as the anatomical reference becomes unclear.
common_causes: Several repetitions or averages were stacked into one file rather than saved separately or averaged into one volume.
A multi-echo or multi-inversion acquisition was written as one file, where BIDS separates the parts with the echo or inv entity.
A different acquisition, such as a quantitative MRI series, was given the T1w suffix. A file collection of that kind has its own suffixes and entities.
A conversion merged several distinct series that happened to share a series description.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Look at the size of the fourth dimension, which tells you how many images were stacked. If they are repetitions, either split them into separate files distinguished by the run entity, or average them into the single volume you intend to use. If they are echoes or inversions, split them and label them with the echo or inv entity. If the acquisition is a quantitative MRI file collection, use the suffix defined for it rather than T1w.

ai_enrichment.description: The number of values in TotalAcquiredPairs does not match the number of control-label pairs listed in the associated aslcontext.tsv. TotalAcquiredPairs holds one value per volume, so its length has to equal the number of volumes it describes.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is a warning: the dataset remains valid BIDS, but the mismatch usually indicates a real bookkeeping mistake. The check is comparing two independent statements about how many volumes the file contains and finding they disagree. One of them is wrong, and the validator cannot tell which.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: When the array length is wrong, there is no correct way to pair its values with the volumes. Software either fails outright or, worse, pairs them by position and silently attributes the wrong parameter to every volume after the first discrepancy. Results computed that way look plausible and are wrong.
example_scenarios: Four dummy volumes are discarded from a run, so the image now has four fewer volumes than TotalAcquiredPairs has values.
common_causes: Volumes were removed from the image after the sidecar was written, for example dummy scans dropped during preprocessing, without the corresponding entries being removed from the array.
The acquisition was stopped early or restarted, so fewer volumes were saved than the protocol planned, while the sidecar still describes the planned acquisition.
The sidecar was copied from a similar run with a different number of volumes.
A single value was written where one value per volume is required, or one value per volume was written where a single value was expected.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Count the volumes in the image itself, then count the values in TotalAcquiredPairs, and establish which of the two reflects what was actually acquired. Correct whichever is wrong rather than padding or trimming the array to make the numbers agree, because padding produces values that are the right length and describe nothing real.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: When a field may hold either one value for the whole file or one value per volume, both forms are legitimate. The mismatch is only between the per-volume form and a volume count, so switching to the single-value form is a valid fix when the parameter really was constant across the acquisition.

ai_enrichment.description: TotalReadoutTime carries a value greater than 10 seconds. BIDS expresses this field in seconds, and a genuine TotalReadoutTime above 10 seconds seconds is rare enough that the validator asks you to confirm it.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is a warning, not an error: the dataset is still valid BIDS and the validator cannot tell a real long value from a unit mistake. It is flagging that the number looks like milliseconds. For most acquisitions TotalReadoutTime falls well under a second, typically a few tens of milliseconds.

A value that is 1000 times too large silently distorts anything derived from it, including slice timing correction, temporal filtering, design matrices and modelling of the haemodynamic response. Nothing downstream will warn you a second time.

common_causes: The value was copied straight from a DICOM header or scanner console in milliseconds. BIDS requires seconds, so the number is 1000 times too large.
A conversion script wrote TotalReadoutTime without applying the unit conversion its source format needed.
The field was filled in by hand from a scanner protocol printout, which usually reports milliseconds.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Check the value against the acquisition protocol. If it was taken from a DICOM header in milliseconds, divide by 1000 and write the result back into the JSON sidecar. If the long value is genuinely correct for this acquisition, leave it as it is: the warning is a prompt to verify, not a defect to remove, and there is no way to suppress it other than correcting the value.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: BIDS states all timing metadata in seconds. Most sources of the same information, DICOM in particular, state it in milliseconds, so this class of mistake is common and worth checking across every timing field in the sidecar rather than only the one reported.

ai_enrichment.description: The sidecar does not carry enough information to determine the total readout time. Either TotalReadoutTime must be given directly, or EffectiveEchoSpacing must be given so it can be derived.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error of missing metadata. It is not that a value is wrong, but that neither of the two accepted ways of stating the readout time is present.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Readout time determines how far susceptibility distortion displaces the image along the phase-encoding axis. Without it, distortion correction cannot compute the size of the correction, only its direction.
common_causes: The conversion did not derive the value, which happens when the source data does not expose the parameters it is computed from.
The field was removed during anonymisation or sidecar editing.
The sidecar was written from a template that omitted it.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Add either TotalReadoutTime or EffectiveEchoSpacing to the sidecar, in seconds. Both can be derived from the acquisition parameters: the echo spacing, the number of phase-encoding lines and the parallel imaging acceleration factor. These are available from the scanner protocol, and many conversion tools will compute them if given the original source files rather than already-converted images.

ai_enrichment.description: The TriggerChannelCount field in the JSON sidecar does not equal the number of rows in the associated channels.tsv whose type column is TRIG. The sidecar and the channel table disagree about how many TRIG channels the recording contains.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is a warning: the dataset is still valid BIDS, but one of the two statements about the recording is wrong and downstream software may read either of them. channels.tsv is the more reliable of the two, because it describes the recording channel by channel, while TriggerChannelCount is a summary that is easy to write once and never update. Treat the table as the truth and the count as the thing to correct, unless you have a specific reason to believe otherwise.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Analysis software uses these counts to decide how to interpret a recording: which channels to load, which to treat as data and which as auxiliary. A wrong count can mean channels are silently dropped from an analysis, or that non-brain channels are analysed as though they were data. It is also the first sign that the sidecar describes a different recording than the one it sits beside, for example after files were copied between sessions.
example_scenarios: A recording is preprocessed, two bad channels are removed and channels.tsv is rewritten from the cleaned data, but the sidecar still declares the original TriggerChannelCount.
common_causes: Channels were added to or removed from the recording, for example by dropping bad channels, and channels.tsv was regenerated while the sidecar TriggerChannelCount was left at its original value.

The type column in channels.tsv does not spell the channel type as BIDS requires. The type MUST be upper case and drawn from the list the standard defines, so a row typed as "trig" or with a vendor-specific name is not counted as TRIG.
The sidecar was copied from another recording in the same study that had a different montage or a different number of auxiliary channels.
Auxiliary channels were counted into the wrong category, for example an eye channel recorded as EEG rather than EOG, so two counts are wrong at once.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Open the channels.tsv beside the recording and count the rows whose type column equals TRIG. If that number is right, set TriggerChannelCount in the JSON sidecar to it. If the number is wrong, the table is what needs correcting: check that each channel's type is spelled in upper case and uses one of the channel types the standard defines, since a misspelled type is not counted. Do not adjust the count to silence the message without establishing which of the two is actually correct.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: Channel types in channels.tsv must be upper case and must come from the set the BIDS standard defines. A type that merely looks right, such as a vendor label or a lower-case spelling, is not recognised and is therefore not counted.

ai_enrichment.description: VolumeTiming and DelayTime are both present in the same sidecar. BIDS treats them as mutually exclusive ways of describing the same acquisition timing, so only one may be given.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This is an error. It is not that one of the two values is wrong; it is that giving both leaves the file describing its timing twice, with no rule saying which description wins.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Downstream software has to choose one. Different tools choose differently, so the same dataset yields different timing depending on what reads it. Removing the redundant field is what makes the timing unambiguous.
common_causes: A conversion wrote every timing field it could derive from the source data, without applying the standard's exclusivity rules.
A field was added by hand to an existing sidecar that already described its timing another way.
A sidecar was merged from two sources, each using a different convention.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: DelayTime describes the gap between the end of one volume's acquisition and the start of the next within a regular repetition time, so it belongs with RepetitionTime rather than with VolumeTiming. When volume times are listed individually, the delays are already implied by the list. Decide which description matches the acquisition and delete the other field from the sidecar. Do not leave both with the intention of being thorough: in this case, more metadata is less information.

The `fsLR` is a surface template.
Additionally, by convention,
`fsLR` is used as shorthand for a **dual template** providing both volumetric and surface
coordinates references,
where the surface template is `fsLR` and the volumetric template corresponds to `MNI152NLin6Asym`.
Surface templates are given at several sampling densities:
164k (used by HCP pipelines for 3T and 7T anatomical analysis),
59k (used by HCP pipelines for 7T MRI bold and DWI analysis),
32k (used by HCP pipelines for 3T MRI bold and DWI analysis), or
4k (used by HCP pipelines for MEG analysis) fsaverage_LR surface reconstructed from the T1w image.

Used by Freesurfer and Connectome Workbench.
